OnlyJobs® : DSSSB Result 2026 How to Check

  • DSSSB (Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board) exam results can be checked easily through OnlyJobs®. Candidates searching for OnlyJobs DSSSB Result 2026 can follow the methods below to check their result, marks, and cutoff details.
  • There are two main methods to check DSSSB results – first through PDF and second by logging into the DSSSB online portal.
  • First : DSSSB Result PDF Method
    In many cases, DSSSB releases the result in PDF format. Candidates need to download the PDF and search their roll number using the Ctrl + F option. If the roll number is found in the list, the candidate is considered qualified.
  • Second : DSSSB Online Portal Login Method
    Some results are available through the DSSSB online portal where candidates can check their scorecard, marks, and detailed result.
  • To login, candidates need to enter:
  • Date of Birth
  • Class 10 Roll Number

This section explains the official process the Board followed between the provisional answer key and the final result, which is important context for understanding why some questions were cancelled or answer keys revised.

Both notices follow the same standard procedure used by UPPBPB for written examinations:

  • The provisional answer key was published on 29 May 2026, and candidates were invited to submit online objections regarding any question or answer option.
  • After the objection window closed, the Board examined each objection and either retained, revised, or cancelled the relevant question.

What Is the Supreme Court of India Law Clerk Result 2026?

This section explains the purpose and scope of the Law Clerk Result 2026 and which examination it belongs to.

The Supreme Court of India Law Clerk Result 2026 is the outcome of the written examination conducted for engaging Law Clerk-cum-Research Associates on a short-term contractual basis for the 2026-2027 term. The recruitment drive was announced for 90 vacancies, and the result determines which candidates qualify for the next stage of selection, which is the personal interview. The result is issued by the Recruitment Cell of the Supreme Court of India and made available through the official website, sci.gov.in.

Supreme Court Law Clerk Recruitment 2026 - Key Dates

This section lists the major milestones of the recruitment cycle in chronological order, from notification to result, so candidates can quickly verify the sequence of events.

Event Date
Notification released 20 January 2026

Written Examination (Part I and Part II) 7 March 2026

Interview shortlist released 17 April 2026

Click Here Supreme Court of India Law Clerk Result 2026

Supreme Court Law Clerk Exam Pattern and Qualifying Criteria

This section explains how the written examination was structured and the minimum marks required to qualify for further stages.

The written examination consisted of two parts. Part I was an objective test conducted online, while Part II was a subjective written test in which the question paper appeared on the computer screen and candidates wrote their answers by hand. Negative marking of 0.25 mark applied for each incorrect answer in the objective section.

To qualify, candidates were required to secure at least 60% marks in Part I and at least 50% marks in Part II. Based on this criteria, 374 candidates qualified the written examination out of all those who appeared.

How to Check and Download the Supreme Court Law Clerk Scorecard 2026

This section explains the process candidates must follow to view and download their individual scorecard for the written examination.

Candidates who appeared in the Law Clerk-cum-Research Associates Examination 2026 could download their individual scorecard from the link provided by the Recruitment Cell. The scorecard remained available for viewing from 20 April 2026 to 4 May 2026. Candidates needed their registration details to log in and access the scorecard, which displayed marks obtained in Part I and Part II of the written test.

  • Visit the official scorecard portal link issued by the Supreme Court Recruitment Cell.
  • Log in using your registration number and other required credentials.
  • View and download your scorecard showing Part I and Part II marks.
  • Save a copy or take a printout for future reference, as the viewing window is time-limited.

Supreme Court Law Clerk Interview Shortlist 2026: 270 Candidates Called

This section covers the interview shortlist released after the written examination result, including the cut-off marks used for shortlisting.

On 17 April 2026, the Recruitment Cell of the Supreme Court of India released the list of 270 candidates shortlisted for interview in the Law Clerk-cum-Research Associates Examination 2026. These candidates secured an aggregate of 243 marks or more in the combined written examination (Part I and Part II) and were arranged strictly in order of merit.

Before finalising this shortlist, the Recruitment Cell also reviewed objections raised against the published answer key. Following this review, one mark each was awarded to all candidates for four specific question IDs, and the revised scores were used in preparing the final merit-based shortlist.

What Shortlisted Candidates Need to Do Next

This subsection outlines the immediate action required from candidates who appear on the interview shortlist.

Shortlisted candidates are required to submit their preferences for the respective chambers of Supreme Court Judges, in order of priority, indicating under whom they wish to work as Law Clerk-cum-Research Associate. The link for submitting these preferences is made available to the 270 shortlisted candidates through the official Supreme Court website. Interview calls are subsequently issued based on each candidate's rank and the preferences submitted.

What Happens After the Law Clerk Result and Interview Shortlist

This section explains the remaining stages in the selection process after the written results and interview shortlist are announced.

The recruitment process for Law Clerk-cum-Research Associates does not end with the written result. After the interview shortlist, the process typically continues as follows:

  • Shortlisted candidates submit chamber preferences for Supreme Court Judges.
  • Interview calls are issued according to merit rank and submitted preferences.
  • Candidates attend the personal interview, which evaluates legal knowledge, drafting, and analytical skills.
  • A final panel of candidates is engaged as Law Clerk-cum-Research Associates for the 2026-2027 contractual term based on combined performance.

Eligibility Criteria for Group Y Medical Assistant Airmen

Eligibility for this post depends on educational qualification and falls into two distinct pathways. This section outlines the academic and age requirements for each.

Educational Qualification

Trade Pathway Eligibility Criteria
Medical Assistant Trade Pass in 10+2 / Intermediate (or equivalent) with Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and English, securing minimum 50% aggregate marks and 50% in English; OR a two-year vocational course in the same non-vocational subjects with identical minimum marks from a recognized board.

  • Medical Assistant Trade (Diploma / B.Sc in Pharmacy pathway):

  • Upper Age Limit: 21 years (additional age relaxation may apply as per the official notification).

Candidates should refer to the detailed notification for specific age relaxation rules applicable to certain categories.

Parameter Standard

Weight Proportionate to height and age, as per IAF standards
Dental Health Healthy gums, good set of teeth, minimum 14 dental points
Visual Standards 6/36 in each eye, correctable to 6/9; refractive error not exceeding +3.50D including astigmatism

How to Download PSSSB Result 2026 PDF

Candidates can check and download the SSSB Punjab Result 2026 PDF for any of the above posts by following these simple steps. The result is published in PDF format and contains roll numbers of all qualified candidates along with the Common Merit List (CML).

  4. Click the link to open the PDF in your browser.
  5. Press Ctrl+F (Windows) or Cmd+F (Mac) to open the search bar and type your Roll Number.
  6. If your roll number appears, you are qualified / selected.
  7. Download and save the PDF for future reference and document verification.

Alternatively, use the direct PDF links provided in the table at the top of this article to save time.

What is a Result - cum-CML (Common Merit List)?

A Result-cum-CML (Common Merit List) published by SSSB Punjab is a combined document that serves two purposes. It announces the result of the written examination and also presents a merit list of all qualifying candidates ranked by their marks. This merit list is used for subsequent selection stages such as counselling, document verification, or appointment.

  • Result: Declares which candidates have passed the written examination.
  • CML (Common Merit List): Ranks all qualifying candidates across categories based on marks obtained.
  • How it is used: Candidates on the CML are called for document verification / counselling in merit order up to the number of available vacancies.
  • Tie-breaking rule: In case of equal marks, the older candidate is generally given preference. If age is also equal, marks in the qualifying examination are considered.

What to Do After Checking the PSSSB Result 2026

Once you have confirmed your qualifying status in the PSSSB Result 2026, the following steps are important to prepare for the next stage of the selection process.

For Qualified Candidates

  • Keep all original documents ready, including educational certificates, category certificate, age proof, Punjab domicile, photo ID, and any other documents mentioned in the original advertisement.
  • Do not submit any fee or documents to unauthorized sources. All communications will be through the official PSSSB website only.
  • Regularly check sssb.punjab.gov.in for notices related to your post and advertisement number.

For Candidates Not in the Result List

  • Check your roll number carefully in the correct PDF for your post and advertisement number.
  • If you believe there is a discrepancy, contact SSSB Punjab through official channels.
  • Stay updated for any supplementary list or provisional list that may be released subsequently.

The merit list contains the roll numbers and names of candidates who have secured the qualifying marks in the Phase-I written exam and have been shortlisted for Phase-II. It is prepared based on:

  • Marks scored in the Phase-I online examination
  • Category-wise reservation norms

Only candidates whose names or roll numbers appear in the merit list will be called for Phase-II testing.

Selection Process After the Agniveer Vayu Result

Once the result is declared, candidates often want clarity on what comes next in the recruitment journey. The Indian Air Force selection process for Agniveer Vayu runs across three structured phases.

Phase-I: Online Written Examination

This stage has already been completed and assessed, and the result declared on 16 June 2026 reflects performance in this phase.

Phase-II: Physical Fitness Test (PFT) and Adaptability Tests

Shortlisted candidates undergo physical fitness checks and adaptability assessments. The expected fitness benchmarks include:

  • Running: 1.6 km within the prescribed time limit (separate timing for male and female candidates)
  • 10 Push-ups within 1 minute (male candidates)
  • 10 Sit-ups within 1 minute for males, 1 minute 30 seconds for females
  • 20 Squats within 1 minute for males; 15 squats within 1 minute for females
  • Adaptability Test-I and Test-II, which evaluate mental agility, decision-making, and suitability for service conditions

Phase-III: Document Verification and Medical Examination

Candidates who clear Phase-II proceed to detailed document verification followed by a medical examination as per IAF medical standards, which includes height, weight, chest measurement, vision, and overall physical fitness checks.

Only candidates who successfully clear all three phases are considered for final selection as Agniveer Vayu.

What Is the SBI Clerk 1st Waiting List 2026?

This section explains the purpose of a waiting list and why SBI releases one after the final result. In short, the waiting list lets SBI fill leftover vacancies without conducting a fresh recruitment cycle.

After SBI declares the final SBI Clerk merit list, some selected candidates do not join, or they resign shortly after joining. To fill these resulting vacancies, SBI maintains a waiting list of candidates who narrowly missed the final cut-off. The 1st Waiting List released on 19th June 2026 is the first such list prepared for this purpose, and it contains the roll numbers of candidates now provisionally selected against these vacant posts.

Why Did SBI Release a Waiting List?

This section explains the reason behind the waiting list, addressing why some candidates are getting a second chance even after the final result was declared.

A waiting list is generated to fill vacancies left vacant due to two main reasons:

  • Non-joining: Some originally selected candidates choose not to join SBI after final selection.
  • Resignation: Some candidates join but resign shortly afterward, freeing up their position.

Rather than running an entirely new selection process, SBI fills these vacancies from the existing pool of candidates who appeared in the merit list but missed selection by a narrow margin.

What Happens After the SBI Clerk 1st Waiting List 2026?

This section explains the next procedural steps for candidates who find their roll number in the list, so they know exactly what to expect.

Candidates whose roll numbers appear in the 1st Waiting List are only provisionally selected. Final confirmation depends on successful document verification and meeting all eligibility conditions specified in the official advertisement. Provisionally selected candidates will be contacted by their respective SBI circles for:

  • Document Verification (DV) scheduling
  • Medical Examination details
  • Joining formalities and reporting date

Candidates called for document verification should keep the following ready:

  • Original educational certificates
  • Valid identity proof
  • Category certificate (if applicable)
  • Domicile certificate (if applicable)
  • Passport-size photographs

If a candidate fails to produce the required documents or does not meet the eligibility criteria, the bank can cancel their provisional selection.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has released the Admit Card / Call Letter for the SEBI Assistant Manager (Officer Grade A) 2025 Recruitment Exercise - Interview Round. Eligible candidates who have cleared the earlier stages of the selection process can now download their SEBI Assistant Manager Interview Call Letter directly from the official SEBI website at https://sebi.gov.in/. The call letter is a mandatory document to carry to the interview venue, and no candidate will be permitted to appear without it.

What Is the SEBI Assistant Manager Admit Card 2026?

The SEBI Assistant Manager Admit Card 2026 is the official interview call letter issued by SEBI to candidates who have successfully qualified the previous rounds of the Officer Grade A (Assistant Manager) Recruitment Exercise 2025. This call letter serves as an entry pass for the interview stage and contains critical information such as the candidate's name, roll number, interview date, time, and venue. Bihar Police Constable Exam Date 2026

This section covers the confirmed examination date, paper structure, and timing as notified by CSBC.

The written examination for Constable recruitment under Advertisement No. 01/2026 will be held on 24 June 2026 (Wednesday) in a single shift across 38 revenue districts of Bihar. As per the official notice, the exam consists of two papers conducted back-to-back with a 30-minute gap between them, and candidates must appear for both papers under a single admit card.

Paper Reporting Time Exam Timing Duration
Paper 1 8:00 AM to 9:00 AM 10:00 AM to 1:30 PM 90 minutes
Paper 2 Immediately after Paper 1 Following Paper 1 with a 30-minute gap 90 minutes

Each paper contains 100 objective-type questions worth 1 mark each, with negative marking of 0.25 marks for every wrong answer. Entry to the exam centre closes one hour before the exam, at 9:00 AM, and candidates are not permitted to leave the hall until both papers are completed and OMR sheets are sealed.

This section outlines the conduct rules and restricted items at the exam centre, as mandated by CSBC for the Constable written exam.

  • Mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, Wi-Fi gadgets, electronic pens, pagers, and smartwatches or any wristwatch are strictly prohibited inside the exam centre.

  • The question booklet cannot be taken out of the exam hall.
  • The OMR answer sheet is prepared in three copies the original, a duplicate, and a carbonless third copy. Only the third (carbonless) copy is given to candidates to take home; the original and duplicate must be submitted.
  • Candidates must separately mark their attendance and biometric details for each of the two papers.

Gauhati High Court Computer Assistant Written Exam Pattern 2026

Understanding the Gauhati High Court Computer Assistant written exam pattern helps candidates prepare strategically. The examination is OMR-based and objective in nature, covering both technical and general aptitude topics. Here is the complete exam pattern for the Computer Assistant post.

  • Exam Mode: OMR-based (Objective Multiple Choice Questions)
  • Total Marks: 120 marks
  • Exam Duration: 2 hours (120 minutes)
  • Negative Marking: 0.25 marks deducted for each wrong answer

Subject-wise Marks Distribution - Computer Assistant

Subject / Section Maximum Marks Remarks

Gauhati High Court Computer Assistant Selection Process 2026

The selection for the Computer Assistant post under Gauhati High Court Recruitment 2026 is carried out in multiple stages. Candidates need to clear each stage to be considered for final appointment. The selection process consists of the following stages:

  1. Stage I - Written Examination: An OMR-based objective test of 120 marks and 2 hours duration. Candidates who clear the minimum qualifying marks in the Assamese section and secure sufficient marks overall proceed to the next stage.
  2. Stage II - Viva-Voce / Interview: Shortlisted candidates from the written examination are called for a personal interview or viva-voce test.
  3. Final Merit List: Based on the combined performance in the written test and viva-voce, a final merit list is prepared and selected candidates are appointed to the post of Computer Assistant.

The city intimation slip contains crucial information about exam city, date, shift timing, and reporting time. This document helps candidates plan their travel and accommodation arrangements before the admit card release. In this article, we provide the direct download link, step-by-step instructions, and all important details about SSC City Intimation Slip 2026.

What is SSC City Intimation Slip 2026?

The SSC City Intimation Slip 2026 is an advance notification document released before the admit card. It provides candidates with essential preliminary information about their examination to help them make necessary travel and accommodation arrangements. The city slip is NOT your admit card but serves as an important reference document.

Key Information Available in City Slip:

  • Allotted exam city and state
  • Scheduled exam date
  • Shift timing (Morning/Afternoon/Evening)
  • Reporting time at exam center
  • Gate closing time
  • Candidate's name and registration number
  • Category (SC/ST/OBC/General/EWS)
  • PwBD status (if applicable)

Important Notice: The city intimation slip is NOT your admit card and does not permit you to appear in the exam. It is only for informational purposes. You must download the admit card separately (available from 15th January 2026) to enter the examination hall.

How to Download SSC City Intimation Slip 2026? (Step-by-Step Guide)

Step 1: Visit Official Website

  • Open your web browser (Chrome, Firefox, or Edge recommended)
  • Visit SSC official website: ssc.gov.in
  • Or use your regional SSC portal if applicable
  • Ensure you have stable internet connection
  • On the homepage, scroll down to "Latest Updates" or "Important Links" section
  • Look for link: "SSC CGL Tier 2 City Intimation Slip 2026" or "Check City Intimation for SSC CGL 2025 (Tier-II)"
  • Click on the city intimation slip download link
  • You may be redirected to a candidate login page
  • Enter your Registration Number (or Username/OTR)
  • Enter your Password (or Date of Birth if applicable)
  • Type the Captcha Code as shown in the image (case-sensitive)
  • Double-check all entered information for accuracy
  • Click on the "Submit" or "Login" button
  • Your city intimation slip will appear on the screen
  • Carefully verify all details displayed
  • Check: Name, Registration No., Exam City, Date, Shift Timing
  • Click on "Download" or "Save as PDF" button
  • Save the file to your computer/mobile device
  • Take a printout of the city slip for reference
  • Save a backup copy in cloud storage (Google Drive/Email)
  • Keep both digital and physical copies safe

Download your city intimation slip as soon as it is released to avoid server overload and last-minute technical issues. The website may experience heavy traffic during peak hours.

When you download your city intimation slip, you will find the following information:

Important Instructions Dos and Don’ts for exam day

Note: The exact exam center address will be mentioned only in the admit card, which will be released on 15th January 2026 (or 2-3 days before your scheduled exam date). The city slip only mentions the exam city name.

Common Issues & Solutions While Downloading City Slip

Issue #1: Unable to Login / Invalid Credentials Error

Solutions:

  • Verify your registration number carefully (no spaces before/after)
  • Check password (case-sensitive) or reset if forgotten
  • Ensure CAPS LOCK is off while entering details
  • Clear your browser cache and cookies (Ctrl+Shift+Del)
  • Try using a different web browser (Chrome, Firefox, or Edge)
  • Use "Forgot Password" link if needed
  • Check your registered email for confirmation

Issue #2: City Slip Not Showing / Page Not Loading

Solutions:

  • Verify if city slip is released for your specific exam date
  • Try downloading during non-peak hours (early morning 6-8 AM or late night 11 PM onwards)
  • Disable VPN, proxy, or ad-blocker extensions
  • Check your internet connection stability
  • Try using mobile data instead of WiFi (or vice versa)
  • Use incognito/private browsing mode
  • Update your web browser to the latest version

Issue #3: Error in Details Displayed on City Slip

Solutions:

  • Contact SSC helpdesk immediately
  • Email to: helpdesk email available on ssc.gov.in with screenshot
  • Call helpline: Check official website for contact (working hours)
  • Keep your registration number and application details ready
  • Explain the exact discrepancy in detail
  • Request for correction before exam date

Issue #4: PDF Download Not Working

Solutions:

  • Take a screenshot of the city slip as backup
  • Try "Print to PDF" option (Ctrl+P then save as PDF)
  • Use a different PDF reader (Adobe Acrobat Reader)
  • Check if pop-ups are blocked in browser settings
  • Ensure sufficient storage space on device
  • Try downloading from different device

Issue #5: Captcha Not Visible or Loading

Solutions:

  • Refresh the page (F5 key)
  • Enable JavaScript in browser settings
  • Disable browser extensions temporarily
  • Use a different browser
  • Clear browser cache completely

City Intimation Slip vs Admit Card - Key Differences

Many candidates confuse city intimation slip with admit card. Here's a clear comparison to understand the differences:

Aspect City Intimation Slip Admit Card / Hall Ticket
Purpose Advance information only for travel planning Mandatory entry document for examination
Release Time 7-10 days before exam date 2-3 days before exam date
Information Provided Exam city, date, shift timing only Complete center address, roll number, photo, signature
Can you enter exam hall? ❌ NO - Not permitted ✅ YES - Mandatory requirement
Contains Photo ❌ No ✅ Yes
Contains Roll Number ❌ No ✅ Yes
Exam Center Address Only city name Complete address with venue details
Use for Travel Booking ✅ Yes - Use for advance planning Can use after release
Barcode/QR Code Usually not present Present for verification
Exam Instructions General instructions Detailed exam day instructions

Critical Warning: You CANNOT enter the examination hall with only the city intimation slip. You MUST download and carry the admit card (available from 15th January 2026) along with a valid photo ID proof to appear for the exam.

Download your SSC CGL Tier 2 City Intimation Slip 2026 immediately from ssc.gov.in and start planning your travel! All the best for your exam!

CBSE CTET September 2026 Exam Eligibility Code Details

CTET Primary Level (Class I to V): Eligibility with Code September 2026
  1. Senior Secondary (or its equivalent) with at least 50% marks and passed or appearing of 2- year Diploma in Elementary Education (by whatever name known) OR
  2. Senior Secondary (or its equivalent) with at least 45% marks and passed or appearing in of 2- year Diploma in Elementary Education (by whatever name known), in accordance with the NCTE (Recognition Norms and Procedure), Regulations, 2002.  OR
  3. Senior Secondary (or its equivalent) with at least 50% marks and passed or appearing in 4- year Bachelor of Elementary Education (B.El.Ed).
  4. Senior Secondary (or its equivalent) with at least 50% marks and passed or appearing in 2- year Diploma in Education (Special Education).
  5. More Eligibility Details Read the Notification

CTET Junior Level (Class VI to VIII): Eligibility with Code September  2026
  1. Graduation and passed or appearing in final year of 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education (by whatever name known).
  2. At least 50% marks either in Graduation or in Post-Graduation and passed or appearing in Bachelor in Education (B.Ed).
  3. Graduation with at least 45% marks and passed or appearing in Bachelor in Education (B.Ed), in accordance with the NCTE (Recognition Norms and Procedure) Regulations issued from time to time in this regard.
  4. Senior Secondary (or its equivalent) with at least 50% marks and passed or appearing in of 4- year Bachelor in Elementary Education (B.El.Ed).
  5. Senior Secondary (or its equivalent) with at least 50% marks and passed or appearing in of 4- year B.A/B.Sc.Ed or B.A.Ed/B.Sc.Ed.
  6. Graduation with at least 50% marks and passed or appearing in  B.Ed. (Special Education)*.
  7. Any candidate having qualified B.Ed. Programme recognized by the NCTE is eligible to appear in TET/CTET. Moreover, as per the existing TET guidelines circulated vide NCTE letter dated 11-02-2011, a person who is pursuing any of the teacher education courses (recognized by the NCTE or the RCI, as the case may be) specified in the NCTE Notification dated 23rd August 2010 is also qualified to appear in the TET/CTET.
  8. Post-Graduation with a minimum 55% marks or equivalent grade and passed or appearing in three-year integrated B.Ed.-M.Ed.

About the HPPSC Assistant Professor Recruitment 2026

This is a consolidated drive covering 22 individual subject-wise advertisements for teaching posts in Himachal Pradesh's government colleges, ranging from Hindi and Chemistry to Tabla and Public Administration. Each subject runs as a separate Online Recruitment Application (ORA) on the HPPSC OTR portal, since vacancies, reservation breakup, and advertisement numbers differ from subject to subject, even though age, fee, and selection rules remain identical across all 22.

HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026 - Subject-Wise Vacancies (369 Posts)

The 369 posts are spread unevenly across 22 subjects, with English (39 posts) carrying the largest share, followed by Chemistry and Hindi (34 posts each), while Dance and Tabla have only 2 posts each. All posts, regardless of subject, carry the same Rs. 35,000/- monthly pay.

Category-Wise Reservation

Every subject's vacancies are further split into UR, SC, ST, OBC, and EWS, with sub-quotas for Ex-Servicemen, Ward of Freedom Fighters, and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities wherever applicable. For instance, the English post (39 vacancies) is divided as UR=16, SC=05, ST=03, OBC=02, EWS=04, with the rest under sub-categories, while smaller posts like Dance and Tabla are entirely unreserved. Candidates should verify the category matrix in their subject's specific notification PDF, as it directly affects age relaxation and cut-off eligibility.

Eligibility Criteria

HPPSC requires a Master's degree with at least 55% marks (50% for SC/ST/OBC and PwBD) in the relevant subject, a qualifying NET/SLET/SET score, and an age between 18 and 45 years as on 1 January 2026. The subject of the Master's degree must correspond to the post applied for.

  • Master's degree with 55% marks (or equivalent grade) in the relevant subject from a recognized university, or an equivalent recognized foreign degree.
  • 5% relaxation (55% to 50%) for SC/ST/OBC (non-creamy layer) and Physically/Visually Handicapped candidates.
  • 5% relaxation for Ph.D. holders who completed their Master's before September 1991.
  • NET (UGC/CSIR) or equivalent SLET/SET is the minimum eligibility condition for the post.
  • Ph.D. holders are exempt from NET/SLET/SET, provided the Ph.D. was awarded in regular mode, evaluated by at least two external examiners, included an open viva-voce, and is backed by at least two published papers (one refereed) plus two conference presentations.
  • Candidates who qualified SET-2026 are also eligible; the window will reopen for them if the SET-2026 result comes after the regular closing date.

The age is calculated as on 1 January 2026, based on the Matriculation certificate. A 5-year relaxation in upper age applies only to Bonafide SC/ST/OBC, Ward of Freedom Fighters, and Persons with Disabilities of HP, and only if the post is reserved for that category in the subject applied for; HP Government employees and Ex-Servicemen get relaxation per separate government instructions.

Application Fee and How to Apply

The application fee is a flat Rs. 600 for all candidates, paid online via Debit Card, Credit Card, UPI, or other digital modes, and is non-refundable and non-transferable once paid. Since each subject is a separate application, the fee must be paid afresh for every subject applied to.

  1. Visit http://www.hppsc.hp.gov.in/hppsc.
  2. Click "Apply Online" on the homepage.
  3. Select "One Time Registration (OTR) for Examinations" and complete registration if new.
  4. Log in to the OTR account and view live advertisements on the dashboard.
  5. Select the relevant subject advertisement (e.g., Hindi – 47/6-2026, History – 48/6-2026) and fill the form.
  6. Upload scanned Matriculation certificate, degree/marksheets, category certificate, and Bonafide HP certificate.
  7. Pay the Rs. 600 fee online.
  8. Confirm the undertaking on document legibility and submit the final application.
  9. Download the confirmation/printout for records.

Once submitted, no corrections or modifications are allowed, so candidates should verify every field before final submission.

Documents Required for Upload

Applications with missing or poor-quality scans are liable to rejection, so candidates should keep the following ready: Matriculation certificate for age proof, degree certificates with all years' marksheets, experience certificate (wherever required), and valid category certificates (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/Ex-Servicemen/WFF/PwBD) in the HP Government's prescribed format. Reserved category candidates additionally need a Bonafide Himachali certificate, and EWS applicants need an Income & Asset Certificate or a BDO-countersigned BPL Certificate along with a non-SC/ST/OBC certificate.

Selection Process

Selection runs through a two-paper written test on the same day, followed by a Personality Test, with final merit based on Paper-II plus interview marks. The process starts with document scrutiny and ends with a 30-mark interview at HPPSC's Shimla office.

Stage Component Details
1 Application Scrutiny Eligible candidates provisionally admitted; rejected candidates get 10 days to represent
2 Paper-I: Screening Test 1-hour MCQ, 100 marks (HP GK-30, National/International Affairs-30, Hindi-20, English-20); qualifying only
3 Paper-II: Subject Aptitude Test (SAT) 3-hour descriptive test, 120 marks, subject-specific syllabus; held same day as Paper-I
4 Document Verification Shortlisting per category-wise zone ratio (1:5 for 11+ posts; 1:5+3 for up to 10 posts)
5 Personality Test 30 marks, at HPPSC office Shimla only; minimum pass 40% General / 30% Reserved
6 Final Merit SAT (120) + Personality Test (30) = 150 marks total

Paper-I is qualifying only and does not count toward merit; candidates scoring zero or negative marks are excluded outright. There is 0.25 mark negative marking per wrong, multiple, or blank answer in objective tests, and the SAT qualifying mark is 45% General / 40% Reserved.

Salary

Selected candidates are engaged as Job Trainees at a fixed Rs. 35,000/- per month, uniform across all 22 subjects, under the Department of Personnel's notification No. Per(AP)-C-B(15)-3/2024 dated 19 July 2025, which governs the job-trainee engagement scheme across HP Government departments.

Important Dates

Event Date
Notification Released 17 June 2026
Online Application Start 17 June 2026
Last Date to Apply Online 14 July 2026, 11:59 PM
Last Date for Fee Payment 14 July 2026, 11:59 PM
Screening Test / SAT Exam To be announced
Personality Test To be announced (HPPSC office, Shimla)

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Applying under the wrong subject advertisement number: With 22 separate codes (34/6-2026 to 55/6-2026), an incorrect subject selection cannot be corrected after submission.
  • Uploading unclear documents: Illegible scanned certificates lead to rejection, so scan at adequate resolution.
  • Submitting without a final review: No corrections are allowed post-submission, so date of birth and category should be double-checked beforehand.
  • Skipping NET/SLET/SET proof upload: Missing this can cause provisional rejection even for otherwise eligible candidates.
  • Missing the answer key objection window: Objections to the Paper-I key must be raised within 5 days of publication with Rs. 100 per question; this window cannot be reopened.
  • Assuming blanket relaxation: Age and qualification relaxations apply only if the post is reserved for that category in the specific subject.

Eligibility Criteria for HSSC CET Group D 2026

Eligibility for this CET cycle is built around two simple pillars - educational qualification and age - but each carries specific conditions that can disqualify an otherwise eligible candidate if overlooked.

Educational Qualification

For all Group-D posts except Sweeper, Chowkidar, and Sweeper-cum-Chowkidar, a candidate must hold:

  • Matriculation from a recognized Board, and
  • Hindi or Sanskrit up to Matriculation as one of the subjects studied.

The notification clarifies that the detailed, post-wise educational qualification (for the specific Group-D posts) will be published separately along with the vacancy details.

Age Limit and Relaxation

A candidate must be not less than 18 years and not more than 42 years of age as on the closing date of registration (3 July 2026). Age relaxation is governed by Haryana Government instructions dated 25 March 2022, and the upper age limit can extend up to 52 years for candidates entitled to combined relaxation benefits.

Unmarried women 5 years

Adhoc/contract/work-charged/daily-wage employees of Haryana Govt. departments Equal to completed years of such service, subject to a maximum age of 52

A repeated candidate note worth flagging: anyone who already registered for CET Advt. No. 1/2022 (held on 5–6 November 2022) or CET Advt. No. 1/2025 (held on 26–27 July 2025) must use that same CET Registration Number rather than creating a fresh one.

How to Apply Online for HSSC CET Group D 2026

Applications are not submitted on a separate HSSC form - everything runs through Haryana's One Time Registration (OTR) system, which is also used for other state recruitment exams.

  1. Visit the official registration portal at onetimeregn.haryana.gov.in.
  2. New applicants register and receive a Registration Number; returning CET 2022/2025 candidates log in with their existing number.
  3. Fill in personal, educational, and category details accurately, since no corrections are allowed after final submission except during the 7–9 July 2026 edit window.
  4. Upload all category-specific scanned documents (see the documents section below).
  5. Pay the applicable fee online through net banking, debit card, or credit card.
  6. Submit the form, then download and retain a printed copy along with the uploaded documents for future reference.

Apply Online - once live on 19 June 2026, the link will be available through onetimeregn.haryana.gov.in.

Application Fee for HSSC CET Group D 2026

Fee payment follows the category-wise structure set under the CET Policy notified on 31 December 2024, with separate concessions based on residency proof and gender.

Candidates who had already applied and paid fee for CET Group C Advt. No. 1/2025 need not pay the fee again for this Group D cycle. Only candidates applying fresh are required to pay, based on the Standard Rate of Rs. 1,000 (or as revised by the Government).

Documents Required for HSSC CET Group D 2026 Application

Every applicant, regardless of category, must upload a common base set of documents, with additional category-specific papers layered on top.

Common documents (all categories):

  • Scanned copy of the Matriculation certificate
  • Latest colour photograph with white background, clearly showing the candidate's name and the date it was taken
  • Scanned signature
  • A signed undertaking as per Annexure VIII of the notification

Category-specific additions:

Category Additional Documents Needed
DSC / OSC Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + DSC or OSC caste certificate
BC-A / BC-B (Non-Creamy Layer) Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + BC-A/BC-B certificate issued on or after 1 April 2026
EWS Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + EWS certificate issued on or after 1 April 2026
Eligible Sports Person (ESP) Haryana Bonafide Resident certificate + Sports Gradation certificate

PwBD Scanned copy of the disability certificate

Only documents uploaded at the time of filling the form are considered for scrutiny - anything submitted later, in any form, will not be entertained.

HSSC CET Group D 2026 Exam Pattern

The CET for Group D is designed as a single-stage, OMR-based screening test rather than a multi-stage exam, making the marking scheme one of the most important things to understand before attempting it.

Feature Detail
Number of Questions 100 MCQs
Total Marks 100
Duration 1 hour 45 minutes
Question Paper Level Secondary Education (Matriculation level)
Language Bilingual - English and Hindi
Mode Offline, OMR-based
Negative Marking for Wrong Answer None
Penalty for Skipped Question -1 mark, but only if the candidate fails to darken the fifth "not attempting" bubble

This last rule is unusual and trips up many candidates: marking a wrong answer carries no penalty at all, but leaving a question blank without filling in the designated fifth circle results in a one-mark deduction. The exam centre, once allotted on the admit card, will not ordinarily be changed.

HSSC CET Group D 2026 Syllabus

The CET syllabus is split into two weighted parts - a larger general-skills component and a smaller Haryana-specific component - and the question paper stays at Matriculation difficulty throughout.

Part A: 75% Weightage

  • General Awareness: India and neighbouring countries, especially History, Indian Polity & Constitution, Art & Culture, Geography; General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
  • Reasoning: Alphabetical order, series, coding-decoding, direction and distance, order and ranking, blood relations, analogy, classification, clock and calendar, mirror/water image, syllogism, sitting arrangement, statement and assumption/conclusion, counting figures, non-verbal series
  • Quantitative Ability: Number system, simplification, decimals, fractions, LCM/HCF, ratio and proportion, percentage, roots, average, profit and loss, discount, simple and compound interest, mensuration, partnership, mixtures and alligation, time and work, time and distance, basic trigonometry, algebra, and geometry
  • English Language: Grammar, spotting errors, fill in the blanks, synonyms and antonyms, spellings, idioms and phrases, sentence improvement, active/passive voice, direct/indirect narration, and tenses
  • Hindi Language: Varna, swar-vyanjan, sangya, sarvanam, visheshan, kriya, kaal, sandhi, samas, paryayvachi-vilom shabd, muhavare-lokoktiyan, and vakya shodhan

Part B: 25% Weightage - Haryana-Specific General Knowledge

This portion covers History, Current Affairs, Literature, Geography, Environment, and Culture of Haryana, along with the state's economy, civics, polity, art, customs, and society.

Minimum Qualifying Marks and Validity of Earlier CET Scores

A general-category candidate needs to score at least 50% in the CET to be eligible, while reserved-category candidates (both vertical and horizontal) get a 10% concession, bringing their qualifying mark to 40%.

For candidates who already cleared the Group D CET held on 12 January 2024 - a score that remains valid until 11 January 2027 - their marks (originally scored out of a maximum of 95) will be mathematically converted into a percentage so they can be merged into the same combined merit list as candidates appearing under the new 100-mark pattern.

It's also worth noting that selection for Group-D posts has changed structurally: under a Government notification dated 12 February 2026, the earlier selection formula (which included up to 10 marks for socio-economic factors such as orphan or widow status alongside the written exam) has been replaced. Selection is now based entirely on CET marks, with no interview at any stage.

HSSC CET (Group D) Syllabus 2026

Reservation Benefits and Certificate Rules

Reservation benefits under this notification are available only to bonafide residents of Haryana State; reserved-category candidates from other states or Union Territories are treated purely as general-category candidates for this recruitment.

BCA and BCB (Non-Creamy Layer)

Certificates must follow the format in Annexure-II and be issued on or after 1 April 2026. Certificates issued for contesting Panchayati Raj elections, or OBC certificates issued for Central Government jobs, are not accepted.

EWS (Economically Weaker Section)

The family's gross annual income must be below Rs. 8 lakh (revised upward from Rs. 6 lakh per the 14 January 2026 instructions), and the family must not own specified assets such as 5+ acres of agricultural land, a 1,000+ sq. ft. residential flat, or immovable property valued at Rs. 1 crore or more. The certificate must be issued on or after 1 April 2026 and is valid only for the financial year it specifies.

DSC and OSC (Deprived and Other Scheduled Castes)

Under instructions dated 13 November 2024, Haryana's existing 20% Scheduled Caste reservation quota is now split equally between Deprived Scheduled Castes (DSC) and Other Scheduled Castes (OSC). If suitable DSC candidates aren't available, the balance posts can go to OSC candidates, and vice versa.

Ex-Servicemen and Freedom Fighter Dependents

Ex-servicemen benefits follow Government Instructions dated 25 May 2026, while reservation for children or grandchildren of Freedom Fighters (paternal or maternal lineage) follows instructions dated 27 October 2021 and 26 April 2022, applicable only when reserved Backward Class or Ex-servicemen posts remain unfilled.

Provisions for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)

Candidates registering under the PwBD category must select the correct disability code at the time of registration: VH (Visual Impairment), HH (Hard of Hearing), OH (Orthopedic, including locomotor disability and cerebral palsy), or MD (Multiple Disability, including autism and intellectual disability).

Scribe and compensatory time facilities are available as follows:

  • Candidates with blindness, locomotor disability (both arms affected), or cerebral palsy can use a scribe without needing a physical-limitation certificate.
  • Candidates in other PwBD categories need a certificate from a Chief Medical Officer, Civil Surgeon, or Medical Superintendent confirming the need for a scribe.
  • The scribe's own qualification must be up to Matriculation only, and the scribe cannot be a candidate in the same examination.
  • All eligible PwBD candidates referred above receive 20 minutes of compensatory time per hour, bringing the total exam duration to 140 minutes instead of 105.

Selection Process for HSSC CET Group D 2026

Since Group-D recruitment has no separate written exam beyond the CET, the process works differently from Group-C recruitment. The Commission shortlists candidates purely on CET marks, then publishes a category-wise merit and waiting list. When actual posts are advertised later, eligible candidates apply electronically to express willingness for that specific post using their existing Registration Number - only the candidate's consent is sought before the Commission recommends names to the appointing department; there is no fresh written test at this stage.

In case of a tie in CET marks, the older candidate gets precedence; if birth dates also match, the candidate whose first name comes earlier alphabetically (in English) ranks higher.

Exam Day Rules and Malpractice Penalties

HSSC enforces strict frisking and conduct rules at every CET centre, and violations carry debarment periods ranging from two to five years depending on severity.

Items strictly barred inside the exam hall include textual material, calculators, pens, geometry boxes, pen drives, mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, smartwatches, wallets, belts, caps, jewellery, and food or water containers. Candidates wearing articles of religious or cultural faith are advised to report at least two hours before the last reporting time to allow for proper frisking.

Type of Malpractice Debarment Period
Leaving the venue uninformed, or removing exam material from the hall 2 years
Misbehaving with staff, obstructing the exam, or submitting fabricated documents 3 years
Forged admit card/ID, copying, possessing electronic gadgets, impersonation, or hacking exam systems 5 years

OMR sheets must be marked only with a ballpoint pen (not a pencil), and any erasing, scratching, or use of whitener detected by the scanning machine leads to outright cancellation of the OMR sheet and candidature.

Who Should Apply for HSSC CET Group D 2026?

This recruitment cycle is suited to candidates who meet the matriculation-plus-language qualification and fall within the eligible age bracket, with a clear path for reserved-category candidates as well.

You should apply if you:

  • Have passed Matriculation from a recognized board with Hindi or Sanskrit as a subject
  • Are between 18 and 42 years of age as on 3 July 2026, or qualify for a relaxation category
  • Are a bonafide resident of Haryana seeking reservation benefits, or are applying as a general-category candidate from anywhere in India, Nepal, or Bhutan

You should reconsider applying if you:

  • Do not hold Matriculation, or did not study Hindi/Sanskrit up to that level
  • Fall outside the 18–42 age band without an applicable relaxation
  • Are a reserved-category candidate from outside Haryana expecting reservation benefits - you will only be considered under the general category

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Several avoidable errors lead to rejection at the scrutiny stage or loss of marks during the exam itself, based directly on the causes of rejection listed in the notification.

  • Uploading a BCA, BCB, EWS, or DSC/OSC certificate dated outside its required validity window
  • Submitting an incomplete document set for your claimed category
  • Registering more than once instead of using an existing CET 2022 or 2025 Registration Number
  • Leaving a question blank without filling the fifth "not attempted" bubble, resulting in an avoidable -1 mark
  • Darkening more than one circle for a single question, which voids that answer entirely
  • Assuming corrections can be made after final submission - they are only possible during the 7–9 July 2026 window
  • Carrying barred items such as mobile phones, watches, or wallets into the exam hall

Why Join SBI as a Probationary Officer?

This section answers why thousands of graduates target the SBI PO exam every year as one of India's most sought-after banking careers. Selected candidates step into leadership-track roles from day one, with the bank highlighting accelerated career progression, nationwide and international postings, structured leadership-development training, and exposure to modern digital banking operations. The role also comes with strong job security, an attractive compensation package, and a clear promotion path that can take meritorious officers up to Top Management Grade over time.

Eligibility for the SBI PO post is built on two pillars: an age limit checked as on a fixed cut-off date, and an academic qualification checked as on a separate, later cut-off date. Candidates must satisfy both conditions independently to be considered eligible for this recruitment.

SBI PO Age Limit 2026: 21 to 30 Years

SBI PO Application Fee 2026

The application fee for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 is Rs 750 for Unreserved (UR), EWS, and OBC candidates, while SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempted from paying any fee. This fee is non-refundable once paid and cannot be carried forward or held in reserve for any other examination, so candidates should confirm their category and details before making the payment.

CIBIL Score Requirement for SBI PO Candidates

A distinctive eligibility condition for this recruitment relates to credit history, since SBI PO is a banking role with financial responsibility. Candidates who have defaulted on repayment under any loan, NBFC, or financial institution arrangement, including credit card dues, and whose accounts reflect adverse credit history in CIBIL or another recognised credit agency, must regularise or repay all outstanding dues on or before the date of joining the Bank. If the adverse status has not been updated in CIBIL records by the joining date, candidates must either get the status updated or produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the lender confirming there are no outstanding dues; failure to do so will render the candidate ineligible and the offer of appointment will be withdrawn. Candidates are advised to check their CIBIL score before applying.

SBI PO Selection Process 2026: Prelims, Mains & Interview

Selection for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 follows a three-phase process: Phase-I Preliminary Examination, Phase-II Main Examination, and Phase-III Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview. Candidates must clear each phase to be considered for the next, and only the marks from Phase-II and Phase-III are carried forward to prepare the final merit list.

Phase-I: SBI PO Prelims Exam Pattern 2026

The Preliminary Examination is an online objective test carrying 100 marks, to be completed in 1 hour, with separate timing for each of its three sections. There is no sectional cut-off in the Preliminary Exam, but a category-wise merit list is prepared based on the aggregate score, and candidates numbering approximately 10 times the vacancies in each category are shortlisted for the Main Exam.

Section No. of Questions Marks Duration
English Language 40 - 20 minutes
Quantitative Aptitude 30 - 20 minutes
Reasoning Ability 30 - 20 minutes
Total 100 100 1 hour

Phase-II: SBI PO Mains Exam Pattern 2026

The Main Examination is conducted online and consists of an Objective Test of 200 marks and a Descriptive Test of 30 marks, taken together in 3 hours 30 minutes. The descriptive paper is administered immediately after the objective test, and candidates must type their answers directly on the computer.

Section No. of Questions Max Marks Duration
Reasoning & Computer Aptitude 40 60 50 minutes
Data Analysis & Interpretation 30 60 45 minutes
General Awareness / Economy / Banking Knowledge 60 60 45 minutes
English Language 40 20 40 minutes
Objective Test Total 170 200 3 hours
Descriptive Test (Email / Situation Analysis / Report or Precis Writing) 3 30 30 minutes
Grand Total 230 3 hours 30 minutes  

Each candidate must score a minimum qualifying mark in every individual section, including the descriptive paper, with sectional cut-offs decided by the Bank based on vacancies. A category-wise merit list is then prepared from the aggregate Main Exam score, and candidates numbering approximately 3 times the category-wise vacancies are shortlisted for Phase-III.

There is also a penalty for wrong answers in both the Preliminary and Main objective tests: for every wrong answer, 1/4th of the marks assigned to that question is deducted, while unattempted questions carry no penalty.

Phase-III: Psychometric Test, Group Exercise & Interview

Shortlisted candidates undergo a Psychometric Test for personality profiling, followed by a Group Exercise (20 marks) and a Personal Interview (30 marks), totalling 50 marks. The Psychometric Test findings are shared with the interview panel to give a fuller perspective on each candidate, and all questions in this test are mandatory.

Final Merit List and Normalisation

The marks from Phase-II (Main Exam, both Objective and Descriptive) and Phase-III (Group Exercise & Interview) are normalised to 100 marks each before being combined into the final merit list; marks from the Preliminary Exam are not added at this stage.

Component Maximum Marks Normalised Marks
Main Examination (Objective + Descriptive) 230 75
Group Exercise & Interview 50 25
Total 280 100

If two or more candidates score identical marks at the cut-off point in the final merit list, they are ranked according to age in descending order, meaning the older candidate is placed higher.

SBI PO Apply Online 2026: Step-by-Step Registration Guide

Candidates can apply for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 only in online mode, from 18 June 2026 to 8 July 2026; no other mode of application is accepted. Before starting, candidates must have a valid personal email ID and mobile number kept active until the declaration of the final result, since all call letters and result-related communication will be sent there.

  1. Visit SBI's official careers portal at https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings (also accessible at https://bank.sbi/web/careers/current-openings) and locate Advertisement No. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09.
  2. Download and carefully read the detailed advertisement PDF before proceeding with registration.
  3. Click Apply Online and open the registration form under "Current Openings."
  4. Keep scanned images ready in advance: your photograph (4.5cm x 3.5cm, 200×230 pixels, 20–50 KB), signature (140×60 pixels, 10–20 KB), left-hand thumb impression (3cm x 3cm, 240×240 pixels, 20–50 KB), and a hand-written declaration (10cm x 5cm, 800×400 pixels, 50–100 KB), all in JPG/JPEG format.
  5. Fill in the application form carefully; you can save a partially completed form, which generates a provisional registration number and password that you must note down to resume later.
  6. Capture a live photograph through your webcam or mobile phone during registration, as this is mandatory in addition to the uploaded photograph.
  7. Recheck every field for accuracy, since no edits are allowed once the form is finally submitted.
  8. Pay the applicable application fee online through Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI; SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempt from the fee.
  9. On successful payment, download and print the e-receipt and application form for your records.
  10. Complete your application well before 8 July 2026 to avoid last-minute technical issues caused by heavy website traffic.

You can also apply directly through the dedicated SBI PO registration link at https://ibpsreg.ibps.in/sbipojun26/.

SBI PO Salary 2026: Pay Scale and CTC

Selected candidates for SBI PO Recruitment 2026 will draw a starting basic pay of Rs 48,480, plus 4 advance increments, in the Junior Management Grade Scale-I (JMGS-I) pay scale of 48480-2000/7-62480-2340/2-67160-2680/7-85920. In addition to basic pay, officers are eligible for Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), City Compensatory Allowance (CCA), Provident Fund, the National Pension System (NPS), Leave Fare Concession (LFC), medical facilities, lease rental facility, and other allowances as per the Bank's prevailing rules. The approximate CTC at the initial pay scale for the Mumbai Centre works out to Rs 21.97 Lacs.

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

Joining, Bond and Probation Period

Selected candidates must complete a basic banking knowledge online course before joining and will be designated as Probationary Officers, placed on probation for two years with continuous performance assessment. At the time of joining, candidates must execute a bond of Rs 2.00 Lacs, committing to serve the Bank for a minimum period of three years; this bond is invoked if the candidate resigns before completing three years of service. Officers who clear the probation assessment standards are confirmed in JMGS-I, and SBI's promotion policy offers a path for high-performing officers to reach senior and top management grades, including opportunities for international postings.

SBI PO Exam Preparation 2026: Strategy, Exam Pattern, Selection Process & Study Plan

Documents and Identity Proof Required at Examination

Candidates must carry specific documents at each stage of the selection process, and missing or mismatched documents can lead to disqualification. At the time of the Preliminary and Main Examinations, candidates must bring a valid photo identity proof such as a Passport, Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Driving Licence, Voter's ID Card, or Bank Passbook with an attested photograph, along with a self-attested photocopy. The notification also specifies that candidates must possess a valid Aadhaar card, as SBI conducts online Aadhaar verification at different stages of the selection process, and biometric verification (photo and thumb impression/IRIS scan) may also be carried out.

For the Main Exam specifically, candidates must bring the duly authenticated Original Preliminary Exam Call Letter along with the authenticated ID proof copy, the Main Exam Call Letter, and two additional photographs identical to the one used during registration; candidates without these will not be allowed to appear. Use of mobile phones or any electronic devices inside the examination or interview premises is strictly banned and can lead to disqualification.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for SBI PO 2026

Many otherwise eligible candidates lose out due to small, avoidable errors during the application process, so it helps to be deliberate at each step. Keep your photograph, signature, thumb impression, and hand-written declaration within the exact pixel dimensions and file-size ranges specified, since uploads outside these limits will trigger an error and block submission; also remember that signatures and the hand-written declaration in capital letters are not accepted.

Avoid waiting until the closing date of 8 July 2026 to register, as heavy website traffic close to the deadline is a common cause of failed submissions, and SBI does not take responsibility for applications that fail to go through for this reason. Double-check your category selection before final submission, since no change of category is permitted at any stage after registration, and incorrectly chosen reserved or unreserved status cannot be corrected later. If an online payment fails or appears incomplete, register again and make the payment afresh rather than assuming the transaction went through, since the fee is strictly non-refundable. Finally, save your provisional registration number and password immediately after saving your form, and keep multiple copies of your registration photograph ready, as these are needed at every subsequent stage of the selection process.

Indian Air Force has published the detailed notification titled “AIR FORCE COMMON ADMISSION TEST (AFCAT‑02/2026) FOR FLYING BRANCH AND GROUND DUTY (TECHNICAL AND NON‑TECHNICAL) BRANCHES / NCC SPECIAL ENTRY / GATE SCORE ENTRY FOR COURSES COMMENCING IN JULY 2027”. Indian Air Force AFCAT 02/2026 - Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must ensure that they satisfy all eligibility conditions of nationality, age, marital status, educational qualification and medical standards as on the prescribed dates. Upper age limit relaxable up to 26 years (born between 02 July 2001 and 01 July 2007) for candidates holding valid and current Commercial Pilot License issued by DGCA (India).

Indian Air Force AFCAT 02/2026 - Type of Commission

Type of commission offered varies by branch and gender.

Permanent Commission (PC) Available for Men & Women; PC officers serve till superannuation in their respective branches.
Short Service Commission (SSC) - Flying Branch Engagement period of 14 years from the date of commissioning for Men and Women.
Short Service Commission (SSC) - Ground Duty (Technical & Non‑Technical) Initial tenure of 10 years with possible 4‑year extension based on service requirements, vacancies, willingness, suitability and merit.
Pension SSC officers are not entitled for pension; PC officers get pension as per rules.

Indian Air Force AFCAT 02/2026 - Application Fee

A non‑refundable examination fee is applicable for AFCAT entry; there is no fee for NCC Special Entry and GATE Score Entry.

Entry Examination Fee
AFCAT Entry (All Branches incl. Tech) Rs. 550/- plus 18% GST (non‑refundable).
NCC Special Entry / GATE Score Entry No AFCAT examination fee.

Indian Air Force AFCAT 02/2026 - Selection Process

The selection process comprises an online AFCAT exam, followed by Air Force Selection Board (AFSB) testing, medical examination and final merit list.

Stage 1 - AFCAT Online Examination

Exam Subject Duration No. of Questions Maximum Marks
AFCAT General Awareness, Verbal Ability in English, Numerical Ability, Reasoning & Military Aptitude Test. 2 Hours (120 Minutes) 100 300

Each correct answer carries 3 marks, each wrong answer attracts a penalty of 1 mark, and no marks are awarded for unattempted questions. The paper is in English only, and normalisation of marks is applied when multiple shifts are conducted.

Stage 2 - Air Force Selection Board (AFSB) Testing

  • Stage‑I: Officer Intelligence Rating Test and Picture Perception & Discussion Test on Day 1; this is a screening stage.
  • Stage‑II: Psychological tests, Group Tests and Personal Interview over the next days for Stage‑I qualified candidates.
  • CPSS: Computerised Pilot Selection System for Flying Branch candidates (once‑in‑a‑lifetime test; CPSS/PABT failures are ineligible for Flying Branch).

Stage 3 - Medical Examination & Final Merit

Candidates recommended by AFSB and found medically fit by the appropriate medical board are considered for training strictly in order of merit and branch‑wise vacancies. The final merit list is based on combined marks of AFCAT (where applicable) and AFSB.

Indian Air Force AFCAT 02/2026 - Exam Pattern & Syllabus

The AFCAT paper is of graduation‑level standard (except Numerical Ability, which is matriculation level) and tests a mix of aptitude and knowledge.

  • English: Comprehension, error detection, sentence completion, synonyms/antonyms, cloze test, idioms & phrases, analogy, sentence rearrangement, one‑word substitution, homonyms.
  • General Awareness: History, Geography, Sports, National & International Organisations, Art & Culture, Personalities, Environment & Ecology, Polity, Economy, Basic Science, Science & Technology, Current Affairs, Defence.
  • Numerical Ability: Fractions, Time & Work, Average, Percentage, Profit & Loss, Ratio & Proportion, Interest, Time & Distance, Area & Perimeter, Probability, Number System, Mixture & Allegation, Squares/Cubes, HCF & LCM, Mensuration, Heights & Distances, Statistics.
  • Reasoning & Military Aptitude: Verbal and Non‑Verbal Reasoning.

An online practice test is available on the IAF AFCAT website.

Indian Air Force AFCAT 02/2026 - Training, Pay & Allowances

Candidates recommended by AFSBs and found medically fit are detailed for training at Air Force Training Establishments based on merit and branch.

  • Training Date & Duration: Training is scheduled to commence in the first week of July 2027; duration is approximately 62 weeks for Flying and Ground Duty (Technical) branches and 50 weeks for Ground Duty (Non‑Technical).
  • Stipend during Training: Flight Cadets receive a fixed stipend of Rs. 56,100/- per month during one year of training (as per 7th CPC matrix).
  • Pay on Commissioning: Flying Officer - Pay Level 10 (Rs. 56,100-1,77,500) plus applicable MSP and allowances as per branch and posting.
  • Insurance: Officers are covered under Air Force Group Insurance Society (AFGIS), with Rs. 1.25 crore cover (on contribution) for death in service and Air Veterans Insurance Cover after retirement for eligible PC/SSC officers.

How to Apply for Indian Air Force AFCAT 02/2026

Applications must be submitted online only through the AFCAT website; no other mode is accepted. Aadhaar Card is mandatory for online registration, and candidates should use valid email ID and mobile number, which must remain active throughout the selection process.

Step‑by‑Step Process (AFCAT Entry):

  1. Visit the official AFCAT website https://afcat.edcil.co.in and read the advertisement and instructions carefully.
  2. Click on the sign‑up/registration link and enter full name, mobile number and email ID, then verify via OTP on email and mobile.
  3. Agree to the declaration, submit the registration form and obtain the system‑generated User ID and Password sent to registered email and mobile.
  4. Login with User ID and Password, click on “Go to Application”, and fill personal details, communication details, qualification details, course preferences and other required fields.
  5. Upload scanned images of recent passport size colour photograph (100-200 KB), signature (80-150 KB), thumb impression (50-100 KB) and live image capture as per specified formats.
  6. Carefully verify all details using “Preview” and then proceed to pay the examination fee of Rs. 550/- + GST (for AFCAT entry only) through online payment gateway (Net Banking, Debit/Credit Card, UPI etc.).
  7. After successful payment and submission, download and print the final submitted application form for future reference.

Applicants should apply well before the last date to avoid last‑minute issues; once submitted, the application cannot be edited, and additional applications against the same Aadhaar will result in only the latest being considered.

Documents to Upload / Produce - AFCAT 02/2026

Scanned Documents to Upload (during Application):

  • Recent passport size colour photograph (100-200 KB; JPG/JPEG).
  • Signature in black ink on white paper (80-150 KB; JPG/JPEG).
  • Thumb impression - Left thumb (male) / Right thumb (female) (50-100 KB; JPG/JPEG/PDF).
  • Live image capture via device camera at the time of application.

Documents to Carry for AFCAT Exam & AFSB:

  • Printout of e‑Admit Card (AFCAT 02/2026).
  • Original Aadhaar Card and a second photo ID (PAN/Passport/Driving Licence/Voter ID etc.).
  • Two passport size colour photographs (same as uploaded).
  • Original and photocopies of Matriculation and 10+2 certificates and mark sheets.
  • Original/provisional Graduation/PG degree and mark sheets (for AFSB).
  • Certificate from College Principal for final year candidates specifying aggregate percentage and likely result date.
  • Original NCC ‘C’ Certificate (for NCC Special Entry) and GATE documents (for GATE Score Entry).
  • NOC from employer for Govt/PSU/Armed Forces personnel, if applicable.

Important Instructions for AFCAT 02/2026 Candidates

  • Candidates must ensure eligibility for the branch(es) they apply for; incorrect information at any stage leads to cancellation of candidature.
  • Use of unfair means or possession of prohibited items (mobile phones, smart watches, electronic devices, study material etc.) inside the exam hall will result in cancellation and debarment from future AFCATs.
  • No request for change of exam centre/date/slot will be entertained; centres may be changed by IAF based on administrative reasons.
  • Serving airmen must apply online like other candidates and also follow service procedures as per AFO 11/2015.
  • Use/possession of narcotics is strictly banned; candidates may be tested for drugs during medicals and training, and those found positive are liable for termination.
  • Permanent tattoos are permitted only on the inner forearms and back of hands (with conditions); non‑permissible tattoos or those with offensive/extremist content lead to rejection.
  • Training is rigorous; candidates should maintain good physical fitness (running, push‑ups, rope climbing, swimming etc.) before reporting to Air Force Academy.

About SDSC SHAR and the Space Central Schools

This section explains who SDSC SHAR is and why it is hiring teachers, which helps candidates understand the nature of the employer before applying.

Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota (SDSC SHAR) is India's spaceport, functioning under the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Department of Space, Government of India. It is located 100 km north of Chennai on National Highway 05, in Tirupati District, Andhra Pradesh. SDSC SHAR operates Space Central Schools at its Sriharikota and Sullurpeta campuses under the NCERT/CBSE curriculum, primarily to educate the children of its employees and supporting personnel. To staff these schools, SDSC SHAR has invited online applications for five categories of teaching posts.

Post-Wise Vacancy Details (10 Posts)

Candidates checking how many posts are open and in which subject can refer to the table below, which lists all five post codes notified by SDSC SHAR along with their reserved category and vacancy count.

Post Code Post Name Vacancies & Category
01 Trained Graduate Teacher (Maths) - to teach Maths & Physics UR-01
02 Trained Graduate Teacher (Science) - to teach Chemistry & Biology SC-01

04 Trained Graduate Teacher (Telugu) ST-01
05 Primary Teacher UR-03, EWS-01, OBC-02 (1 OBC backlog)

Of the six Primary Teacher vacancies, one post is identified for PwBD (LDCP) backlog vacancy. If a suitable PwBD (LDCP) candidate is not found, the post will be offered to a candidate with any other benchmark disability except blindness, and if still unfilled, it will revert to the vertical reservation category. All posts are currently temporary in nature but are likely to continue.

Eligibility Criteria for Each Teaching Post

Each post carries a distinct qualification requirement linked to the subject taught. The table-style breakdown below summarises the core academic and teaching-eligibility requirements for every post code.

TGT (Maths) - To Teach Maths and Physics

Candidates need a four-year NCTE-recognised integrated degree with at least 50% marks (subject + B.Ed component), OR a Bachelor's/Honours degree with 50% marks plus a B.Ed degree from an NCTE-recognised institution (alternatives include a 3-year integrated B.Ed-M.Ed or a 1-year B.Ed Special Education from RCI). Candidates must also have qualified CTET Paper-II and be able to teach in Hindi and English. Applicants must have studied Mathematics as a main subject for at least 3 years/6 semesters, Physics for at least 1 year/2 semesters, and one of Chemistry/Electronics/Computer Science/Statistics for at least 1 year/2 semesters. Candidates with B.Sc (Hons.) in Physics or Chemistry are not eligible for this post.

TGT (Science) - To Teach Chemistry and Biology

The qualification pattern mirrors TGT (Maths): a four-year integrated degree or a Bachelor's/Honours degree (50% marks) with Chemistry, plus a B.Ed degree, along with a qualifying CTET Paper-II score. Candidates must have studied Biology/Life Science/Botany/Zoology as a Honours or main subject for at least 3 years/6 semesters, combined with Chemistry, Botany, or Zoology as applicable for at least one year or two semesters.

TGT - Work Experience Teacher (WET)

This post requires a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or Electronics & Communication Engineering with at least 50% marks, along with a B.Ed degree (50% marks) from an NCTE-recognised institution, ability to teach in Hindi and English, and knowledge of computers. One year of practical workshop/factory experience is desirable but not mandatory.

TGT (Telugu)

Candidates need a Bachelor's degree with Telugu as the main subject (or one of three equal optional subjects), a BOL in Telugu, or a Postgraduate degree in Telugu, combined with a B.Ed with Telugu methodology or Telugu Pandit Training. Candidates must have passed State TET or CTET Paper-II with Telugu as one of the chosen subjects.

Primary Teacher

Eligible candidates need Senior Secondary/Intermediate (10+2) with 50% marks plus a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education, OR Class XII with 50% marks plus a 4-year B.El.Ed, OR Class XII with 50% marks plus a 2-year RCI Diploma in Special Education. A qualifying score in CTET Paper-I and the ability to teach in Hindi and English are also required.

Across all posts, Hindi working knowledge is necessary, and candidates claiming equivalent qualifications must produce documentary evidence at the time of the Skill Test.

  • SC/ST/Disability/Ex-Servicemen certificate (as applicable) - PDF, under 1 MB.
  • Essential qualification documents - PDF, under 1 MB.
  • No Objection Certificate (if employed in Government/PSU/Autonomous body).

The photograph and signature uploaded must be clear and legible; failure to meet this requirement leads to cancellation of candidature. Uploaded documents are verified at the Skill Test stage, and mere admission to the Written Test does not guarantee selection.

Selection Process: Written Test and Skill Test

SDSC SHAR shortlists and selects teachers through a two-stage process - a written exam followed by a practical skill demonstration - explained below with the exact marking scheme.

Written Test (CBT)

The Computer Based Test checks both the theoretical and practical knowledge of candidates across the prescribed syllabus. For Primary Teacher, TGT (Maths), TGT (Science), and TGT (WET), the paper carries 180 marks split into four parts - Languages (20), General Awareness/Reasoning/Computers (20), Education & Leadership Perspective (40), and Subject Specific (100). For TGT (Telugu), the 180-mark paper covers General English/Awareness/Reasoning (20), Education Perspectives (20), Pedagogy (40), and Telugu Language & Literature (100).

Post Subject-Wise Question Split Minimum Qualifying Marks
TGT (Maths) 50% Maths + 50% Physics 40% each subject; 50% aggregate
TGT (Science) 40% Biology + 30% Chemistry + 30% Physics 40% each subject; 50% aggregate

Based on Written Test performance, candidates are shortlisted for the Skill Test, generally in a 1:5 ratio with a minimum of 10 candidates category-wise.

Skill Test

The Skill Test is purely qualifying in nature, evaluated out of 100 marks, with a minimum qualifying score of 60%. It is a chalk-and-board based test where each candidate is given a subject-related topic and must demonstrate subject knowledge and teaching ability by conducting a mock class.

Final Merit and Tie-Breakers

Final selection is based purely on Written Test marks among candidates who clear the Skill Test, with empanelment done as per the number of notified vacancies. In case of a tie, the academic score of the essential qualification (PG/Graduation/Senior Secondary, as applicable) is the first tie-breaker, followed by the candidate's age (senior candidates get preference) as the second tie-breaker.

(ICSIL) is inviting online applications for 65 Nursing Officer posts on a contractual outsourced basis, for deployment at Rajiv Gandhi Super Specialty Hospital (RGSSH), Tahirpur, Delhi. ICSIL Nursing Officer Recruitment 2026 Notification Out

ICSIL has released the official notification for Nursing Officer recruitment under Advertisement No. ICSIL/RC/10-A/RGSSH/NURSING OFFICER/2026-27, dated 17 June 2026. The notification covers 65 posts of Nursing Officer to be deployed on a purely contractual/outsourced basis at Rajiv Gandhi Super Specialty Hospital, an autonomous institute under the Government of NCT of Delhi. Candidates should note that this is a notably short recruitment cycle, with the entire online application process confined to a three-day window starting 20 June 2026.

  • Download ICSIL Nursing Officer Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF

ICSIL Nursing Officer Recruitment 2026 Overview

Particulars Details
Recruiting Organisation Intelligent Communication Systems India Ltd. (ICSIL)

Important Dates to Remember

This recruitment runs on a tight three-day application schedule, so candidates need to track every date carefully. The notification itself was issued on 17 June 2026, while the online application portal opens four days later at 6:00 PM on 20 June 2026. Candidates must complete their application well before the portal closes at 6:00 PM on 23 June 2026, since no extension has been indicated in the notification.
