ICSIL Nursing Officer Recruitment 2026 - Vacancy Details

ICSIL has notified a single post category for this recruitment, with all 65 vacancies falling under the designation of Nursing Officer. There is no further category-wise or department-wise vacancy split mentioned in the notification, so candidates applying for this post are competing for the full 65 positions together, subject to the eligibility and shortlisting criteria laid out below.

Post Name Number of Vacancies
Nursing Officer 65

Eligibility Criteria: Qualification, Age Limit and Experience

Eligibility for the Nursing Officer post is built around three requirements: a recognised nursing qualification, a minimum of five years of relevant post-qualification experience, and an upper age limit of 35 years. Candidates must also possess basic computer knowledge, and registration with the Delhi Nursing Council becomes mandatory at the time of joining, not at the time of applying.

Particulars Details
Educational Qualification B.Sc. Nursing from a recognised institute, OR equivalent qualification with a Certificate in General Nursing Midwifery (GNM) from a recognised institution; basic knowledge of computer required
Age Limit Up to 35 years
Post-Qualification Experience Minimum 5 years of experience as a Nursing Officer is mandatory
Mandatory at Joining Registration with the Delhi Nursing Council

The notification also specifies preference criteria that can influence shortlisting among eligible applicants. Candidates with hands-on experience in ICU, OT, or Cath Lab settings, or in a 200+ bedded Super Specialty Hospital, will be given preference, and so will candidates holding a higher educational qualification in the field of nursing care beyond the minimum B.Sc. Nursing or GNM requirement.

Registration Fee

There is no separate application fee tied specifically to this post; instead, ICSIL operates a portal-wide one-time registration fee. Candidates must pay Rs 590 (non-refundable) to register on the ICSIL website before they can apply to any job listed there, including this Nursing Officer post. This fee is a one-time payment for portal access rather than a recurring or post-specific charge, and it must be paid before the application can be submitted.

ICSIL Nursing Officer Recruitment 2026 - Salary and Pay

Selected Nursing Officers will receive a monthly remuneration of Rs 70,942, as specified in the notification. The notification does not mention a pay level, pay matrix, or any separate allowance structure beyond this fixed monthly figure, so candidates can treat Rs 70,942 per month as the consolidated remuneration for this contractual engagement.

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

ICSIL Nursing Officer Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Selection for the Nursing Officer post follows a two-stage process: shortlisting based on document scrutiny, followed by an interview or interaction with the deploying department. If the number of eligible applicants disproportionately exceeds the number of available positions, ICSIL reserves the right to apply any criteria it considers fit and rational to shortlist candidates for the interview stage.

Shortlisting is carried out by verifying each candidate's age, qualification, and experience against the prescribed eligibility criteria, after which shortlisted candidates undergo an interaction or interview with the department. Depending on the position, the selection process may also include a skill test or written test, and mere appearance in the interview does not guarantee selection.

The decision of the interview panel or selection committee on all matters is treated as final and binding, and the overall selection criteria are based on the marks obtained in academic qualifications combined with a suitability assessment. Finally selected candidates are considered for deployment on a contractual/outsourced basis for a fixed period, or until the contract expires, or until regular incumbents join the posts - whichever happens first. ICSIL has also clarified that it does not guarantee deployment of all shortlisted candidates, and no TA/DA is paid for attending the interaction or document verification.

ICSIL Nursing Officer Recruitment 2026 - Apply Online

Candidates can apply for this recruitment only through the online mode on the ICSIL website, since no other method of application is accepted. The application portal opens at 6:00 PM on 20 June 2026 and closes at 6:00 PM on 23 June 2026, giving candidates a narrow three-day window to register, build their profile, and submit the application before access closes.

  1. Visit the official ICSIL website www.icsil.in and go to the Career section.
  2. Open the Current Job section and refer to the "How to apply for current Jobs" link for portal-specific guidance before starting.
  3. Pay the one-time registration fee of Rs 590 (non-refundable) to activate your ability to apply for jobs on the portal.
  4. Build or update your candidate profile by entering complete educational qualification details, starting from High School through to your highest qualification, along with your work experience.
  5. Ensure your profile matches the eligibility criteria specified for the Nursing Officer post - qualification, age, and experience - since the system checks your profile against these criteria before allowing you to apply.
  6. Submit your application within the window from 6:00 PM on 20 June 2026 to 6:00 PM on 23 June 2026; incomplete applications will be summarily rejected.
  7. Keep checking the ICSIL website regularly for any corrigendum or notification updates related to this vacancy.

Documents Required at Verification and Interview

Candidates shortlisted for interaction or interview must be ready with original documents, since the notification is specific about what is needed and what happens if documents are missing.

  • Original documents for Date of Birth, Educational Qualification, and Experience, as per the eligibility criteria - without these, candidates will not be allowed to appear for the interview or interaction.
  • One set of self-attested photocopies of all relevant documents.
  • Two passport-size photographs.
  • Proof of name consistency: the details in the application form must match the candidate's Class 10th Certificate, PAN Card, and Aadhaar Card. If the candidate's name has changed since Class 10th, documentary evidence of the name change must also be furnished at the time of interaction or document verification.

Also Read: TIFR Recruitment 2026 - Apply Online for 35 Posts, Last Date 4 July 2026

Security Deposit and Refund Terms

A distinctive feature of this engagement is a salary-linked security deposit, which candidates should factor into their financial planning before joining. ICSIL deducts fifteen (15) days' salary as a security deposit, recovered in two parts - 50% in the first month and 50% in the second month of engagement. This deposit is refunded to the candidate along with savings bank interest, but only after two conditions are met: a No Dues Certificate is received from the client department, and the candidate has completed all contractual liabilities with ICSIL as specified in the appointment letter.

Key Terms and Conditions to Know

Beyond eligibility and pay, a few service conditions in the notification directly affect how this role works day to day. The engagement is purely contractual and temporary for a fixed period, and it does not create any claim for regular appointment within ICSIL or the deploying department; selected candidates are engaged under a specific project or scheme, with statutory compliances applying as per the laws of the land.

Although the post is for deployment at Rajiv Gandhi Super Specialty Hospital, the notification states that the place of deployment may be anywhere in Delhi/NCR, and selected candidates may be required to work in shifts or on a rotational basis as per departmental requirement, with no extra conveyance paid by ICSIL. Canvassing in any form - including seeking recommendations, lobbying through intermediaries, or attempting to gain favour through political or personal means - will lead to immediate disqualification from this recruitment and may also affect eligibility for future opportunities with ICSIL. ICSIL further reserves the right to accept or reject any application without assigning a reason, and to withdraw the advertisement at any time without notice.

Who Should Apply

This post suits candidates who already hold a B.Sc. Nursing degree, or an equivalent qualification with a GNM certificate, and who have completed at least five years of post-qualification experience working as a Nursing Officer, while still being within the 35-year age limit. Candidates with prior exposure to ICU, OT, or Cath Lab environments, or experience in a 200+ bedded Super Specialty Hospital, hold a clear advantage in shortlisting, as do those with additional nursing qualifications beyond the minimum requirement.

Candidates should hold off on applying if they do not yet have the mandatory five years of post-qualification experience as a Nursing Officer, if they are above 35 years of age, or if they are not in a position to register with the Delhi Nursing Council by the time of joining, since this registration is a non-negotiable condition for taking up the post.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying

Given the unusually short three-day application window, the biggest risk for candidates is running out of time, so it helps to register on the ICSIL portal and pay the Rs 590 fee as early as possible rather than waiting for the final day. When filling in the profile, enter education details starting from High School onward exactly as they appear on certificates, since mismatched or incomplete academic history is a common reason profiles fail to match the eligibility criteria for a post.

Double-check that your name is entered identically across your application, Class 10th Certificate, PAN Card, and Aadhaar Card before submitting, since any unexplained mismatch can cause problems at the document verification stage; if your name has changed since Class 10th, keep the supporting legal document ready in advance. Keep at least one full set of self-attested photocopies of every relevant document and two passport-size photographs prepared well before any call for interaction, since missing originals at verification can result in a candidate not being allowed to appear at all. Finally, avoid any form of canvassing or attempts to seek recommendations during the process, since the notification treats this as grounds for immediate disqualification, and keep revisiting the ICSIL website periodically in case a corrigendum is issued.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Indian Air Force has released two separate recruitment notifications inviting online applications for Agniveervayu Intake 02/2027 (under the Agnipath Scheme) and Airmen Group 'Y' (Non-Technical) Medical Assistant Trade for Intake 02/2027. Online registration for both notifications opens on 06 July 2026 and closes on 26 July 2026, with the online examination scheduled for 22-23 September 2026. While Agniveervayu is open to unmarried male and female Indian candidates for a four-year engagement, the Airmen Medical Assistant trade is open only to male Indian/Gorkha (Nepal) candidates for a 20-year regular cadre tenure. Applications must be submitted through the official CASB portal at iafrecruitment.edcil.co.in.

IAF Agniveervayu Intake 02/2027 - Eligibility Criteria

Agniveervayu eligibility is divided across age, marital status, and educational qualification requirements specific to Science and Non-Science streams.

Age Limit for Agniveervayu

Candidates born between 01 July 2005 and 01 January 2010 (both dates inclusive) are eligible to apply. If a candidate clears all stages of selection, the upper age limit on the date of enrolment must not exceed 22 years.

Marital Status (Agniveervayu)

Only unmarried male and female candidates are eligible. Candidates must undertake not to marry during the four-year engagement period; female candidates must additionally undertake not to become pregnant during this period, as pregnancy or marriage during service can lead to dismissal.

Educational Qualification for Agniveervayu

Stream Qualification Required
Science Subjects 10+2/Intermediate with Maths, Physics & English (50% aggregate + 50% in English) OR 3-year Diploma in Engineering (Mechanical/Electrical/Electronics/Automobile/Computer Science/Instrumentation/IT) with 50% marks OR 2-year Vocational Course with Physics & Maths (50% marks)
Other than Science 10+2/Intermediate in any stream (50% aggregate + 50% in English) OR 2-year Vocational Course (50% aggregate + 50% in English)

Candidates eligible under Science Subjects may also opt to appear for both Science and Other-than-Science papers in a single sitting while registering.

Domicile Categories for Agniveervayu

Candidates must select one domicile category at the time of registration, which cannot be changed later, as shortlisting and the Provisional Select List are prepared state-wise:

  • Permanent Domicile: Permanent residents of districts of the State/UT, supported by a Domicile Certificate from a Gazetted Revenue Officer.
  • COAFP-I: Children of currently serving Air Force personnel posted in the relevant State/UT.
  • COAFP-II: Children of retired/discharged/deceased Air Force personnel residing in the State/UT for a minimum of one year.

IAF Airmen Group Y Medical Assistant 02/2027 - Eligibility Criteria

This trade has two qualification routes - one for 10+2 candidates and another for Diploma/Pharmacy graduates - each with a different age bracket.

  • Diploma/Pharmacy Route: Passed 10+2/Intermediate with PCB & English (50% aggregate, 50% English) PLUS a Diploma/B.Pharma/B.Sc in Pharmacy with minimum 50% marks, along with valid registration from the State Pharmacy Council or Pharmacy Council of India (PCI) at the time of enrolment.

IAF Recruitment 2026 - Stipend & Benefits

Pay structures differ significantly between the two postings, reflecting their different service models - Agniveervayu under the Agnipath Scheme versus a regular 20-year Airmen cadre.

Agniveervayu Pay Package

Year Monthly Package In-Hand (70%) Agniveer Corpus Contribution GoI Contribution
1st Year ₹30,000 ₹21,000 ₹9,000 ₹9,000
2nd Year ₹33,000 ₹23,100 ₹9,900 ₹9,900
3rd Year ₹36,500 ₹25,550 ₹10,950 ₹10,950
4th Year ₹40,000 ₹28,000 ₹12,000 ₹12,000

On completion of four years, Agniveervayu receive a one-time Seva Nidhi package of approximately ₹10.04 lakh (excluding interest), along with a non-contributory life insurance cover of ₹48 lakh during the engagement period. They are not entitled to gratuity, pension, or Provident Fund contributions, and do not receive Ex-Servicemen (ESM) status after discharge. Up to 25% of each batch may be offered the opportunity to apply for the regular Airmen cadre based on performance.

Airmen Medical Assistant Pay & Allowances

  • Training Stipend: ₹14,600 per month during training.
  • Post-Training Salary: Starting gross emoluments of minimum ₹26,900 per month (including Military Service Pay), plus applicable Dearness Allowance.
  • Other Allowances: Transport Allowance, CPMA, Leave Ration Allowance, Children Education Allowance, HRA, and more.
  • Leave: 60 days annual leave + 30 days casual leave per calendar year.
  • Insurance: Group Insurance cover of ₹62.5 lakh at a premium of ₹3,200/month.
  • Job Role: Training in nursing and first-aid, management of medical stores/dispensaries, and ward supervision duties.

IAF Selection Process 2026: Exam Pattern

Both posts follow a three-phase selection process - an online written test, physical/adaptability tests, and a final medical examination.

Phase I: Online Written Test

Post/Stream Duration Subjects
Agniveervayu (Science) 60 minutes Physics, Mathematics, English
Agniveervayu (Other than Science) 45 minutes English, Reasoning & General Awareness
Agniveervayu (Both Streams) 85 minutes Physics, Mathematics, English, RAGA
Airmen Medical Assistant 45 minutes English, Reasoning & General Awareness

Marking Scheme (both posts): +1 mark for each correct answer, 0 for unattempted questions, and -0.25 for each wrong answer. Marks may be normalised to adjust for variation in difficulty across exam sessions, and candidates must qualify in each subject/paper individually.

Phase II: Physical Fitness & Adaptability Tests

Shortlisted candidates undergo the Physical Fitness Test (detailed above) followed by two written Adaptability Tests assessing suitability for military life and ability to adjust to Air Force working conditions and environments.

Phase III: Medical Examination

Candidates who clear Adaptability Test-II undergo a detailed medical examination by the Air Force Medical Team, including blood haemogram, urine tests, biochemistry profile (blood sugar, cholesterol, kidney & liver function), chest X-ray, and ECG. Candidates declared unfit may appeal via an Appeal Medical Board by depositing ₹40.

Application Fee

Both notifications carry the same non-refundable examination fee, payable online after submitting the application form.

Payment can be made via Net Banking, Debit Card, Credit Card, or UPI. The fee is non-refundable under any circumstances, including for duplicate or rejected applications.

How to Apply for IAF Agniveervayu/Airmen Recruitment 2026

Applications must be submitted entirely online in two steps through the CASB portal.

  1. Visit the official portal: iafrecruitment.edcil.co.in
  2. Step I (Registration): Enter personal and contact details, then click "Generate OTP." Verify both mobile number and email ID using the OTPs received.
  3. Agree to the terms & conditions, re-verify entered details, and click "Submit" to receive your User ID and Password via email/SMS.
  4. Step II (Application Form): Log in and click "Go To Application" to fill in personal, communication, and qualification details.
  5. Upload scanned photograph, signature, parent's signature (if under 18), and left thumb impression as per specified size/format guidelines.
  6. Capture a live photo via webcam for face-match verification.
  7. Preview the form, correct any errors, and click "Submit."
  8. Pay the examination fee of ₹550 + 18% GST through the payment gateway.
  9. Print and retain a copy of the final submitted application form for future reference.

Candidates must indicate five preferred examination city choices while filling the application. Once submitted, the application cannot be withdrawn, and the fee is non-refundable.

Direct Link to Apply

Documents Required for Phase II Testing

Shortlisted candidates must carry original documents along with self-attested photocopies for verification at the Airmen Selection Centre (ASC):

  • Colour printout of Phase-II Admit Card and the filled application form
  • Eight passport-size colour photographs (same as used in registration)
  • Matriculation passing certificate and marksheet
  • 10+2/Intermediate/Diploma/Vocational passing certificate and marksheets
  • Diploma/B.Pharma/B.Sc Pharmacy certificate (Medical Assistant Diploma route only)
  • Domicile/COAFP Certificate (Agniveervayu) or SOAFP Certificate, if applicable (Medical Assistant)
  • Original Phase-I Admit Card bearing Air Force seal and invigilator's signature
  • NCC 'A'/'B'/'C' Certificate, if applicable
  • HB pencil, eraser, sharpener, glue stick, stapler, and a black/blue ball pen

Bank of Baroda has notified 65 vacancies spread across 12 distinct positions, all within the Corporate and Institutional Credit Department. The largest share goes to the AVP II-Relationship Manager post, which alone accounts for 30 vacancies covering the Credit Lite, Conglomerate, MNC, Corporate Banking, and Real Estate segments. The AVP I-Credit Lite/MNC/Real Estate/Conglomerate post carries 7 vacancies, while the DVP-Senior Relationship Manager post has 12 vacancies. The three Vice President posts and the two Deputy Vice President head-of-unit posts each carry a single vacancy.

Bank of Baroda has also stated that only candidates willing to serve anywhere in India should apply, since posting will depend entirely on the bank's requirement at any of its offices or branches across the country.

Bank of Baroda Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Apply Online

Applications for this recruitment can be submitted only through the online mode on Bank of Baroda's official website - no offline or postal applications are accepted. The application window is open from 16 June 2026 to 06 July 2026, and registration is complete only once the application fee is successfully paid through the online payment gateway. Candidates can access the application form directly at www.bankofbaroda.bank.in/Career.htm, under the Career section's "Current Opportunities" page on www.bankofbaroda.bank.in.

  • Direct Link to apply Bank of Baroda Professionals Recruitment 2026

Key Roles and Responsibilities

A few common themes run across most of these positions. The Vice President and Deputy Vice President-level Relationship Head and Senior Relationship Manager roles centre on growing and managing the bank's existing corporate relationships in their specialised segment - real estate, MNCs, credit-lite clients, or conglomerates - sourcing new-to-bank corporate clients, cross-selling fee-based products such as forex and cash management services, and building account plans with opportunity-income analysis while keeping risk exposure within the bank's Exposure Risk Framework. The Transaction Banking roles (Head-Product Sales, Senior Product Sales Manager, and Product Sales Manager) focus on selling trade, forex, and cash management products, managing transaction banking client relationships, and driving fee income and CASA balances. The AVP-level Conglomerate/Real Estate and Credit Lite roles concentrate on credit appraisal, risk evaluation, and timely account monitoring, while the DVP-Head Market Intelligence Unit role is centred on gathering and summarising market and industry intelligence to provide competitive insights to management. Across all positions, the bank has reserved the right to modify or add to these responsibilities at any time.

Application Fee

Bank of Baroda has set a two-tier, non-refundable application fee for this recruitment. Unreserved (UR), EWS, and OBC candidates must pay Rs 850 (inclusive of GST), plus applicable payment gateway charges, while SC, ST, PWD, Ex-servicemen/DESM, and Women candidates pay Rs 175 (inclusive of GST), plus payment gateway charges. The fee can be paid online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI. It is payable irrespective of whether an online test is eventually conducted and irrespective of whether the candidate is shortlisted for an interview, and once paid, it will not be refunded under any circumstances.

In-Hand Salary Calculator 2026

Contract Tenure, Remuneration and Credit Score Requirement

These are fixed-term contractual roles, and the tenure depends on the grade. For AVP I and AVP II, the initial contract runs for 5 years from the date of joining and can be renewed at the bank's discretion, subject to satisfactory performance, for one additional period of up to 5 years. For VP and DVP, the initial contract is for 3 years and can be extended in increments of 1 year each, provided the total engagement does not exceed 5 years. In every case, the engagement automatically ends at contract expiry unless renewed, and it cannot continue beyond the candidate reaching 60 years of age.

Remuneration is not fixed in the notification - the bank states it will be decided based on the selected candidate's qualifications, experience, overall suitability, last drawn salary, and the prevailing market benchmark for the position, and the place of posting will depend on the bank's requirement at any of its offices or branches in India.

A distinctive eligibility condition for this recruitment is credit history: candidates must have a CIBIL score of 680 or above at the time of joining, and the bank has explicitly stated that candidates who have defaulted on loan or credit card repayments, or against whom adverse reports exist with CIBIL or other credit-rating agencies, will be deemed ineligible for appointment - a check the bank can apply at any stage, including after joining.

Selection Process

Selection proceeds through Application Scrutiny, followed by an Online Test, Psychometric Test, or any other test the bank considers suitable, and then a Personal Interview along with compensation negotiation for those selected. The Psychometric Test and/or Interview assess a candidate's personality, communication, clarity, problem-solving ability, efficiency, and willingness to work anywhere in the country. To qualify in the Personal Interview, a candidate must score at least 60% for the Unreserved category and 55% for Reserved category candidates, though the bank reserves the right to revise this cut-off. If multiple candidates tie at the cut-off mark, they are ranked in descending order of age, meaning the older candidate ranks higher.

Call letters will be sent only to the email ID registered in the online application - no hard copies will be sent by post or courier - so candidates must keep that email account active and check it regularly. At the interview, candidates must carry a valid photo ID such as a PAN card, passport, driving licence, voter's card, or Aadhaar card with photograph; a Ration Card will not be accepted as identity proof for this recruitment, and candidates who have legally changed their name must produce the original Gazette notification or affidavit reflecting the new name.

How to Apply: Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Visit the Bank of Baroda website www.bankofbaroda.bank.in (or directly www.bankofbaroda.bank.in/Career.htm) and go to the Career section's "Current Opportunities" page.
  2. Register using a valid personal email ID and contact number that you can keep active throughout the recruitment process, since all call letters and updates will be sent there.
  3. Fill in the online application form carefully - no field can be edited once you click Submit - and ensure your name is spelt exactly as it appears on your certificates and mark sheets.
  4. Upload your bio-data, scanned photograph (200×230 pixels, 20-50 KB), and signature (140×60 pixels, 10-20 KB) in JPG/JPEG format, along with PDF copies of your eligibility documents.
  5. Pay the applicable application fee online using a Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI through the integrated payment gateway.
  6. After successful payment, download and print the system-generated e-receipt and application form for your records; if a transaction fails, register again and make the payment afresh rather than assuming the first attempt succeeded.
  7. Complete the process well before 06 July 2026, since the bank has advised against waiting until the last date to avoid login failures caused by heavy website traffic.

Documents Required (Upload and Interview)

Two separate sets of documents matter here - what must be uploaded with the online application, and what must be physically produced at the interview.

Documents to upload (PDF format, A4 page size, file size not exceeding 500 KB each):

  • Resume
  • Date of Birth proof (10th mark sheet/certificate)
  • Educational certificates (all relevant mark sheets and certificates scanned into a single PDF)
  • Work experience certificates, if applicable
  • Caste/Category certificate, if applicable
  • PWD certificate, if applicable

Documents to carry to the interview (originals plus a self-attested photocopy):

  • Printout of the valid interview call letter and the system-generated online application form
  • Proof of date of birth (birth certificate or SSLC/Class X mark sheet showing DOB)
  • Photo ID proof (PAN, passport, driving licence, voter's card, or Aadhaar with photograph - a Ration Card is not accepted)
  • Semester/year-wise mark sheets and the final degree/diploma certificate
  • Caste certificate in the prescribed Government of India format for SC/ST/OBC/EWS candidates (the OBC certificate must include the non-creamy-layer clause and be issued within one year of the date of advertisement)
  • Disability certificate from the District Medical Board for PWD candidates, along with scribe details if a scribe was used
  • Discharge book, pension payment order, and rank proof for Ex-servicemen candidates
  • A No Objection Certificate from the current employer for candidates serving in Government, Quasi-Government, or Public Sector roles, including nationalised banks
  • Certificate of eligibility from the Government of India for candidates from Nepal, Bhutan, the Tibetan-refugee category, or the specified person-of-Indian-origin categories
  • Proof of work experience such as appointment letters, salary slips, relieving letters, and CTC break-up documents

Bank of Baroda has also appended ready-to-use certificate formats for SC/ST, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer), Persons with Disabilities (single and multiple disability), and EWS candidates as annexures to the notification; candidates applying under these categories should get their certificates issued in this prescribed format from the competent authority.

Troubleshooting and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Keep your scanned photograph between 20-50 KB and your signature between 10-20 KB, both in JPG/JPEG format - files outside this range, or in the wrong format, will trigger an error and block submission. Sign only in your normal handwriting and never in capital letters, since the bank has specified that signatures in capital letters will not be accepted, and any mismatch between your call-letter signature and your interview-day signature can lead to disqualification.

If an online payment fails or you are unsure whether it went through, do not assume it succeeded - register again and complete the payment, since the fee is non-refundable. Use an updated browser and a stable internet connection while filling the form, and avoid waiting until the last day or last few hours before 06 July 2026, since heavy website traffic close to the deadline is a common cause of failed submissions. Always download and save your acknowledgement number, e-receipt, and printed application form immediately after payment, as these are needed for future reference and at the interview. Finally, double-check every field - especially your name, category, and date of birth - before clicking Submit, since no corrections are allowed after the online application has been submitted.

BPCL Experienced Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Age Limit

Age limits vary by post and are reckoned as on 01-04-2026. Upper age limit indicated is for General (UR) and EWS candidates. Age relaxations are applicable as per Presidential Directives for reserved categories. The maximum age of the candidate should not exceed 55 years (for posts with absolute cap) or not exceed General age limit + 10 years (cumulative relaxation cap) as applicable to the respective post.

Category Age Relaxation
General (UR) / EWS As specified per post (34 / 38 / 42 / 46 / 50 years)
SC / ST 5 years relaxation as per Presidential Directives
OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years relaxation as per Presidential Directives
PwBD 10 years relaxation as per Presidential Directives
Ex-Servicemen / Commissioned Officers 5 years (subject to rendering minimum 5 years’ Armed Forces service)
Cumulative Cap (all relaxations combined) Maximum of 10 years cumulative relaxation (or absolute cap of 55 years, whichever applies to the post)

BPCL Experienced Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

The application fee is applicable for all positions. Fee once paid will NOT be refunded under any circumstances. Chargeback cannot be claimed for any reason. Payment must be completed online; no other mode is accepted.

Category Application Fee
General (UR) / OBC-NCL / EWS / Ex-Servicemen Rs. 1,180/- (Application fee Rs. 1,000/- + GST @ 18% i.e. Rs. 180/-) + payment gateway charges if applicable (Non-Refundable)
SC / ST / PwBD NIL (Exempted)
Payment Mode Online only - Debit Card / Credit Card / UPI / Net Banking

BPCL Experienced Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

The multi-stage selection process will be adopted based on the number of applications received for each profile. Final selection is subject to document verification, performance in all selection stages, and Pre-Employment Medical Examination.

Stage 1 – Application Screening

Applications will be screened on the basis of years of relevant work experience, educational qualification, and other eligibility criteria as specified for each profile.

Stage 2 – Computer Based Test (CBT)

Part Section Details
Part I General Aptitude Verbal Ability, Quantitative Aptitude and Logical Reasoning
Part II Professional Knowledge Questions related to the area of specialization of the applied profile

Stage 3 – Case Based Discussion / Group Task / Personal Interview

Candidates shortlisted in the CBT (category-wise and discipline-wise merit list) will be called for Case Based Discussion and/or Group Task and/or Personal Interview. Document verification shall be conducted before this stage. Provisional selection will be based on relevant work experience, on-the-job achievements, and overall performance across all selection stages.

Stage 4 – Pre-Employment Medical Examination

Provisionally selected candidates must clear a Pre-Employment Medical Examination conducted by BPCL’s authorized doctor / nominated hospital as per OISD-GDN-166 guidelines. Medical fitness decision shall be final and binding. Reference for medical examination does not mean final selection.

BPCL Experienced Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Emoluments / Pay Scale

Selected candidates will be placed in appropriate grades (E2 to E8) and pay points based on profile, qualification, experience, and performance in selection. CTC indicated is at the minimum of the pay scale for metro city postings.

CTC includes Basic Pay, Dearness Allowance (IDA pattern), HRA, Perks & Allowances, Retirement Benefits (DPE guidelines), and Performance-Related Pay. Additional benefits include medical coverage for self and dependants, annual leave entitlements, housing loan, education loan, furniture-on-hire, conveyance allowance, and communication expenses.

How to Apply for BPCL Experienced Professionals Recruitment 2026

Candidates shall apply online only; no other mode of application will be accepted. Candidates must read the detailed advertisement carefully before applying. All details entered in the online form will be treated as final and no changes will be entertained after submission.

Documents Required to be Scanned and Uploaded (PDF format):

  • Date of Birth Proof (Class 10th / DOB Certificate)
  • Educational Qualification Proof - Consolidated Marksheet AND Degree / Diploma Certificate (both mandatory)
  • Service Certificate / Work-Experience Certificate(s) from each organization on their letterhead, signed/stamped by authorized representative, showing: Name, Designation, Length of Service, Date of Joining, Date of Separation (if applicable), Nature of Employment (Full-time / Part-time), Detailed Nature of Work, and Current Basic Salary and CTC
  • Relevant Category / Caste Certificate (SC / ST / OBC-NCL / EWS / PwBD / Ex-Servicemen) - issued for appointments under Government of India
  • Recent Color Passport Size Photograph (not older than April 2026)
  • Scanned copy of Signature (signature in CAPITAL LETTERS will NOT be accepted)
  • Latest three salary slips from current organization (scanned together in a single PDF file)

Additional Documents to be Produced at the time of Selection Process / Document Verification:

  • Call Letter / Admit Card along with a valid photo identity proof in original and self-attested photocopy
  • Caste Certificate in prescribed Government of India format (for SC/ST candidates)
  • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate in prescribed Government of India format (for OBC-NCL candidates); self-undertaking to be submitted at time of Personal Interview
  • Income and Asset Certificate issued by Competent Authority valid for FY 2026-27 (for EWS candidates); must be submitted at the time of interview
  • Disability Certificate issued by a Competent Authority as per RPwBD Act, 2016 (for PwBD candidates)
  • Educational qualification certificates and mark sheets
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC) from employer - mandatory for candidates presently employed in Central/State Government, Autonomous bodies, and PSUs

Apply Online at: www.bharatpetroleum.in → CAREERS → CURRENT JOB OPENING → APPLY ONLINE

For queries: Email - [email protected] (mention Application ID in the subject line). Candidates are NOT required to send printout of application or any other documents in hard copy to BPCL.

BPCL Experienced Professionals Recruitment 2026 - Important Instructions

  • Only Indian Nationals are eligible to apply.
  • All eligibility criteria - age, qualification, and experience - are reckoned as on 01-04-2026.
  • Candidates can apply for only one profile. Candidates are advised to submit only one application; in case of multiple applications, only the latest one shall be considered as final.
  • Percentage of marks is calculated on the basis of total marks obtained in all semesters/years in all subjects. Rounding off of percentage is not allowed.
  • Experience gained only after the date of declaration of result of the qualifying degree will be considered. Short-term trainee experience (summer/winter internships during degree) will not be counted.
  • All qualifications must be from AICTE approved / UGC recognized University / Deemed University. Equivalent percentage for CGPA/OGPA must be indicated and supported by a certificate from the University.
  • OBC candidates belonging to ‘Creamy Layer’ are not entitled for OBC-NCL reservation; they must apply as General. OBC-NCL certificate should clearly indicate non-creamy layer status.
  • Candidates presently employed in Central / State Government, Autonomous bodies, PSUs must produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer at the time of selection process.
  • All future communications will be through e-mail only. The email ID and mobile number must remain valid for at least one year. BPCL will not be responsible for non-delivery due to invalid email ID.
  • No email confirmation will be sent on successful registration or fee payment. Candidates must take a printout of the payment acknowledgment for future reference.
  • 3rd AC train fare reimbursement is admissible for CBT for outstation SC, ST & PwBD candidates. 2nd AC train fare is admissible for all outstation candidates appearing in the Interview (distance of not less than 30 km). This is not applicable for candidates already in Central / State Government Services / PSUs.
  • Corrigendum / Addendum, if any, will be published on the official BPCL website only - https://www.bharatpetroleum.in/ - candidates must check regularly.
  • BPCL reserves the right to cancel / restrict / enlarge / modify / alter the recruitment process at any stage without notice.
  • Canvassing in any form at any stage will lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • Court of jurisdiction for any dispute will be at Mumbai.
  • All applications are accepted through the online portal only. This activity has NOT been outsourced by BPCL to any agency/individual. Applicants are advised to beware of fraudulent agencies/individuals.

TIFR Recruitment 2026 - How to Apply

Applications for TIFR Recruitment 2026 must be submitted online only at tifr.res.in. No offline or postal applications will be accepted. Government/Semi-Government/PSU employees, if called for the selection process, must produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer.

  1. Visit the official TIFR website at tifr.res.in.
  2. Navigate to the Careers / Recruitment section.
  3. Click on Advertisement No. 2026/6 and read the full notification carefully.
  4. Click "Apply Online" for the relevant post.
  5. Register and fill in all personal, educational, and experience details accurately.
  6. Upload scanned copies of photograph, signature, and relevant certificates.
  7. Submit the online application before 4 July 2026.
  8. Take a printout of the completed application form for future reference.

Candidates called for the selection process must bring originals along with copies of the following documents:

  • Valid photo identity proof (Aadhaar Card / Voter ID / PAN Card / Passport / Driving Licence)

  • EWS certificate valid preferably for the current financial year

Salary & Appointment Terms

Candidates wondering about appointment duration can note that for posts at Sr. Nos. 1 to 7 and 12 to 17, the initial appointment will be for 3 years including a 1-year probation period. Continuation beyond 3 years is subject to comprehensive performance review; upon successful review, the appointment continues till superannuation at age 60. Post No. 30 (Project Administrative Assistant) is a temporary, non-pensionable contract appointment, renewable annually up to a total of 3 years. All other selected candidates (Posts 1-29) will be governed by the National Pension System (NPS) unless already covered under CCS (Pension) Rules 1972.

Candidates selected for posts at Sr. Nos. 12 to 17 and 22 to 29 will be required to work on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays and must be prepared for shift duties as per institutional requirements.

Who Should NOT Apply

  • Candidates who have completed only a part-time or correspondence degree where the notification requires a full-time degree.
  • OBC candidates without a valid Non-Creamy Layer certificate for the current financial year.
  • Candidates who cannot produce grade-to-percentage conversion certificates from their university, where applicable.
  • Candidates already in government service who are unable to obtain an NOC from their employer before the selection stage.
  • Candidates for Security Guard posts who do not meet the prescribed physical standards (height, chest, eyesight).

📄 Complete Details & Notification

If you are a postgraduate with expertise in fields like Artificial Intelligence, Cyber Security, Climate Finance, Quantum Technology, or Economic Research, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has opened a rare and prestigious opportunity. Under Advertisement No. RBI/TMD1/YP/06/2026-27/01 dated June 15, 2026, RBI is seeking 12 Young Professionals (YP) to work directly within its Central Office Departments (CODs) in Mumbai on short-to-medium-term policy assignments.

This is not an ordinary government job. The RBI Young Professional programme places selected candidates at the center of India's monetary policy, financial regulation, and technology governance framework. With a monthly stipend of ₹1,50,000, a contract tenure of up to 5 years, and direct exposure to top-level policy work, this engagement stands apart from conventional public sector roles.

The last date to apply is July 6, 2026. Applications must be submitted via email only.

  • [Apply Online] – Send your application to [email protected]
  • [PDF Download Link] – Download the official notification: Advt. No. RBI/TMD1/YP/06/2026-27/01 from www.rbi.org.in

Before diving into the details, here is a complete quick-reference summary of the RBI YP Recruitment 2026 for candidates assessing their fit.

What Is the RBI Young Professional Programme?

The RBI Young Professional programme is a unique initiative by the Reserve Bank of India designed to bring domain specialists into the central bank's functioning on a contractual basis. Unlike recruitment for regular officer grades, this programme targets individuals with specialized postgraduate or technical expertise who can contribute meaningfully to short-to-medium-term policy-related research and analytical assignments.

Selected YPs work within RBI's Central Office Departments in Mumbai, gaining direct exposure to India's most consequential financial, monetary, and regulatory policy decisions. The engagement is intended to enrich both the Bank's analytical capacity and the professional development of the selected candidates. It is not a pathway to permanent employment at RBI, but it is widely regarded as an extraordinary professional experience in the Indian financial policy ecosystem.

This section lists every available Young Professional position in RBI's 2026 recruitment drive, along with the respective post code and the Central Office Department where the selected candidate will be placed.

Post-wise Eligibility and Job Profiles: Complete Breakdown

Every RBI YP post has its own educational qualification requirements, desirable experience profile, and a distinct job profile. Understanding these differences is critical before applying. Applying for the wrong post or ignoring the post code in your email subject line could result in rejection.

1. YP0626DOS01 – Cyber Security and Information Technology Risk

Department: Department of Supervision, Central Office, Mumbai

This role is designed for specialists who can help RBI assess technology risks, digital resilience, and cybersecurity threats across the regulated financial sector.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate degree or equivalent in Cyber Security / Information Security / Computer Science / IT / Data Science / AI or a related field.
  • Desirable Qualifications & Certifications: CISSP, CISM, CEH, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, AWS/Azure Security; published research in IT, Cybersecurity, or Public Policy journals.

Desirable Experience:

  • Cyber security, technology risk management, digital regulation, or fintech
  • Cloud security, cyber resilience, digital transformation projects
  • Experience with financial institutions, regulators, CERTs, or tech companies

What You Will Do: Conduct policy research on cyber security and digital resilience; draft framework documents; analyze cyber incidents and threat intelligence trends; support AI/ML, cloud security, and data governance projects.

2. YP0626DOS02 – Policy Analytics (DoS)

Department: Department of Supervision, Central Office, Mumbai

This data-heavy role requires candidates who can transform complex supervisory data into actionable analytical outputs using advanced tools.

  • Essential Qualification: B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech in Computer Science/IT, or Master's degree in Statistics/Data Science.

Desirable Technical Skills:

  • Excel (Power Query, Power Pivot, VBA macros, automation)
  • Power BI (Advanced DAX, interactive dashboards, drill-through functionality)
  • Python (Pandas, NumPy, ETL workflows, automated reporting)
  • Statistics (regression analysis, forecasting, hypothesis testing, predictive modelling)
  • MIS Automation and large multi-source data management

What You Will Do: Extract and analyze supervisory datasets; develop Power BI dashboards; automate recurring MIS reports using VBA and Python; prepare analytical notes and policy briefs for senior management; support RTI/legal matters through structured data review.

3. YP0626DOR01 – Climate Change Risk and Sustainable Finance

Department: Department of Regulation, Central Office, Mumbai

With climate-related financial risks gaining regulatory prominence worldwide, this role positions the selected candidate at the frontier of ESG and sustainable finance regulation in India.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's degree or PG qualification in Climate Change Studies / Environmental Science / Environmental Management / Climate Finance / Sustainability / Economics / Financial Economics / Finance / Statistics / Econometrics / Data Science / Public Policy / Disaster Management / Natural Resource Management / related quantitative disciplines.
  • Desirable Certifications: FRM (GARP), SCR (GARP), ESG-related certifications.
  • Desirable Skills: Knowledge of physical and transition climate risks; understanding of ESG frameworks; Python, R, SQL, Excel, or data visualization tools.
  • What You Will Do: Climate risk research and analysis; policy support and regulatory framework development; climate stress testing; ESG and sustainable finance work; preparation of reports and policy notes; stakeholder engagement and capacity building.

4. YP0626DOR02 – Credit Risk Analytics & Regulatory Policy

Department: Department of Regulation, Central Office, Mumbai

This post is aimed at quantitatively strong candidates who can contribute to credit risk regulation, macroprudential analysis, and evidence-based policy development.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's degree or equivalent in Economics / Econometrics / Statistics / Finance / Mathematics / Data Science / Financial Engineering or related quantitative disciplines.
  • Desirable Qualification: PhD in Finance, Economics, or Statistics; or published research in credit risk or financial stability.
  • Desirable Experience: Risk modelling in financial institutions or credit rating agencies; experience with Python and large datasets; familiarity with ECL/IFRS-9, credit bureau data, BCBS and FSB regulatory standards.
  • What You Will Do: Frame and review credit risk regulations; identify regulatory gaps; support evidence-based policy; analyze international regulatory developments; develop analytical frameworks for assessing the impact of regulatory policies.

5. YP0626DPS01 – Payment Ecosystem

Department: Department of Payment and Settlement Systems, Central Office, Mumbai

This role calls for candidates who can track and analyze developments in India's rapidly evolving payment ecosystem, including cross-border payment architectures.

Essential Qualification (any one):

  • PG degree in Economics / Statistics / Finance / Commerce / Public Policy / Data Science
  • B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech
  • Chartered Accountant (CA)

Desirable Experience: Payment systems, cross-border payments, public policy, or financial markets.

What You Will Do: Monitor market intelligence from international bodies (CPMI, FATF, BIS); undertake primary and secondary research on global payment architectures; generate analytical reports for international forums; statistical modelling of payment flow data.

6. YP0626DPS02 – Policy and Research in Domestic & Cross-Border Payment Systems

Department: Department of Payment and Settlement Systems, Central Office, Mumbai

This position supports RBI's top management with policy notes, research briefs, and market intelligence covering both domestic and international payment developments.

Essential Qualification (any one):

  • PG degree in Economics / Statistics / Finance / Commerce / Public Policy / Data Science
  • B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech
  • Chartered Accountant (CA)

Desirable Experience: Public policy, payment systems.

What You Will Do: Prepare notes and briefs for RBI's top management on payment system policy; track domestic and international payment ecosystem developments; gather market intelligence from CPMI, FATF, BIS; contribute to research and thematic studies on payment systems.

7. YP0626DEP01 – Policy and Research (DEPR)

Department: Department of Economic and Policy Research, Central Office, Mumbai

This is one of the most academically demanding posts in the RBI YP 2026 recruitment, designed for candidates with strong economics research credentials.

  • Essential Qualification: Master's or PhD in Economics, with at least one course paper in Mathematics, Statistics, or Econometrics during the Master's programme.
  • Desirable Qualification: Authored at least one paper in a reputed journal ranked B or above.
  • Desirable Experience: Economic research; experience with STATA, EViews, Python, or R.
  • What You Will Do: Review research papers and reports on policy and regulatory matters; prepare concise summaries and background notes for RBI's top management; support senior leadership in meetings and presentations.

8. YP0626FIN01 – Artificial Intelligence

Department: FinTech Department, Central Office, Mumbai

As AI transforms the financial sector, RBI seeks a specialist who can shape its approach to AI governance, ethics, and regulatory oversight.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate/technical/professional degree in AI / Computer Science / Public Policy / Data Science or a related discipline.
  • Desirable Knowledge: AI governance, machine learning concepts, data ethics, emerging technology policy frameworks.
  • Desirable Experience: AI research, technology policy, data analysis; exposure to ethical AI frameworks, regulatory research, or public policy projects.
  • What You Will Do: Analyse emerging AI technologies; develop policy recommendations on ethics, governance, data privacy, and responsible AI adoption; support regulatory research and stakeholder consultations; assist in strategy formulation for AI-driven innovation ecosystems.

9. YP0626FIN02 – Quantum Technology

Department: FinTech Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This highly specialized and forward-looking role places a candidate at the cutting edge of India's quantum technology policy landscape.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate/technical/professional degree in Quantum Computing / Physics / Electronics / Computer Science / Technology Policy.
  • Desirable Knowledge: Quantum technologies, cybersecurity implications, innovation policy research.
  • Desirable Experience: Quantum technology research, emerging technology analysis, quantum computing applications, or cybersecurity research.
  • What You Will Do: Conduct research on quantum computing, communication, and cybersecurity trends; assist in developing strategic frameworks for quantum ecosystem development; support standards-setting and international collaboration initiatives.

10. YP0626FMO01 – Data Analysis

Department: Financial Markets Operations Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This role suits a candidate who can translate financial market data into policy-relevant insights, particularly in the money market domain.

  • Essential Qualification: Post Graduation in Statistics / Economics with Econometrics as a subject.
  • Desirable Qualifications: CFA, FRM; proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
  • Desirable Experience: Econometrics; published research; banking dealer experience; money market exposure.
  • What You Will Do: Perform data analysis to support policy research; track domestic and global currency and yield movements; analyze money market rates on a daily basis.

11. YP0626FMR01 – Financial Markets

Department: Financial Markets Regulation Department, Central Office, Mumbai

A role for quantitatively oriented professionals who can harness analytical tools to study and interpret financial market behavior for regulatory purposes.

  • Essential Qualification: Postgraduate degree in Economics / Operations Research / Finance / Statistics / Mathematics.
  • Desirable Experience: Any area related to financial markets.
  • What You Will Do: Study and analyze financial market data using cutting-edge analytical tools in close coordination with the regulatory function.

12. YP0626CEP01 – Data Analytics and Policy Research

Department: Consumer Education and Protection Department, Central Office, Mumbai

This role focuses on using data science and machine learning to understand consumer complaint trends and translate them into policy inputs for RBI's leadership.

  • Essential Qualification: B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech, or Postgraduate degree in Mathematics / Statistics / Computer Science / Economics / Data Analytics with knowledge of statistical tools and Power BI.
  • Desirable Skills: Python, R, or SQL for automation, machine learning, and large dataset handling.
  • What You Will Do: Data mining and analytics using AI/ML tools; systematic classification of consumer complaints and trends; process automation of report generation; development of interactive real-time dashboards; preparation of quality policy inputs for RBI's top management.

Who Can Apply? General Eligibility Criteria for RBI YP 2026

Candidates must satisfy the following baseline conditions to be considered for any of the 12 Young Professional positions at RBI. These are non-negotiable and checked at the time of document verification.

  • Nationality: Must be an Indian citizen.
  • Age Limit: Must be above 21 years and not more than 30 years of age as on July 6, 2026. The notification does not mention any age relaxation for reserved categories under this recruitment.
  • Educational Qualification: Must meet the post-specific eligibility criteria as detailed in Annexure-III of the official notification. All qualifications must be from a recognized institution in India or abroad. In cases of similar or alternative qualifications, RBI retains sole authority to determine equivalency.
  • Agreement to Terms: Candidates must agree to the Terms and Conditions of Engagement as specified in the notification.
  • Application Mode: Must apply via email in the prescribed proforma (Annexure-VI of the official notification).

Each post has its own essential qualification. Meeting the general age criterion alone does not guarantee eligibility - always check the post-specific educational requirement before applying.

Monthly Stipend and Terms of Engagement

Understanding what this role offers - and what it does not - is essential before applying. RBI's YP engagement is a contractual position with a generous stipend but with clearly defined boundaries.

Remuneration

A fixed monthly stipend of ₹1,50,000 will be paid throughout the engagement period, subject to applicable tax deductions. No additional allowances, HRA, or benefits are provided over and above this stipend.

Contract Duration

The initial contract tenure is 3 years, which may be extended by mutual agreement for a total period not exceeding 5 years. The extension decision is based solely on the Bank's assessment of the YP's performance and is at RBI's discretion.

Nature of Engagement

This is a contractual, full-time engagement - not a regular or permanent appointment. The YP will have no claim to any regular or permanent position at RBI by virtue of this engagement. There is no employer-employee relationship between RBI and the YP.

Leave Policy

YPs are entitled to 15 days of leave per calendar year, accrued on a pro-rata basis from the date of joining. Leave cannot be carried forward to the next year. Absence beyond this entitlement is treated as leave without pay, with a proportionate deduction from the monthly stipend. Unauthorized absence for 8 or more consecutive working days without valid reason may lead to contract termination.

Termination and Notice Period

Either party may terminate the contract with 3 months' notice. However, during the first 6 months of the initial tenure, the contract may be terminated by either side without any notice period.

Other Conditions

  • Place of engagement is Mumbai; no residential accommodation will be provided by RBI
  • No part-time work for any private or public body is permitted during the engagement without prior written permission from RBI
  • YPs must produce a medical fitness certificate and a satisfactory police verification report on selection
  • A code of conduct agreement and secrecy undertaking must be signed on joining
  • In the event of death, injury, or illness during tenure, neither the YP nor their dependents are entitled to compensation or employment from RBI

How to Apply for RBI Young Professional 2026 – Step-by-Step

The application process for RBI YP 2026 is entirely email-based. There is no online portal, no registration system, and no walk-in interview. Every step must be followed precisely to avoid rejection.

Step 1 – Download the Application Proforma: Download Annexure-VI from the official notification document available at www.rbi.org.in. Fill it out completely. Fields marked with asterisk (*) are mandatory.

Step 2 – Prepare Your Documents: Compile all the following in PDF format:

  • Duly filled application proforma (Annexure-VI) with recent colour photograph (3.5 x 4.5 cm) pasted
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Degree certificates for essential and desirable qualifications (provisional certificate acceptable if the degree is pending)
  • Statement of Interest (explaining why you are applying for the specific post)
  • A sample of academic or policy writing
  • A reference/recommendation letter from a professional referee (preferably from your current/previous employer or academic institution)

Step 3 – Check the Email Specifications:

  • All documents must be in PDF format only - other formats may be blocked by RBI's security filters
  • Total attachment size must not exceed 5 MB
  • The email body must be concise (one or two lines) and unconditional - no additional statements

Step 4 – Format the Email Subject Line Correctly:
The subject line must follow this exact format: "YP Application – [Post Code] – [Your Full Name]"
Example: YP Application – YP0626FIN01 – Ramesh Kumar

Step 5 – Send the Application:
Email your complete application to [email protected] before the deadline.

Step 6 – Applying for Multiple Posts:
If you wish to apply for more than one position, send a separate email for each post. Each email must include a complete, independent set of all required documents.

  • [Apply Online] – Send your application email to [email protected]
  • [PDF Download Link] – Download the official notification and Annexure-VI application proforma from www.rbi.org.in

Last Date: July 6, 2026

Selection Process for RBI YP 2026

Submitting a complete and eligible application is only the first step. The selection process for RBI Young Professionals involves multiple stages, and meeting the minimum eligibility is not a guarantee of progression.

Stage 1 – Preliminary Screening: A screening committee reviews all received applications against the eligibility criteria and the quality of supporting documents. The Bank reserves the right to limit the number of candidates called for interview.

Stage 2 – Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates will be required to submit and verify original documents related to age, educational qualifications, and experience.

Stage 3 – Interview: Shortlisted candidates will receive an interview call letter via email only. No physical call letters will be sent by post. Candidates must make their own travel and accommodation arrangements for the interview.

Reserve List: RBI maintains a reserve list of suitable candidates, valid for one year from the date of publication of the selection list.

RBI's decision regarding shortlisting, interview, and all aspects of engagement is final. No correspondence will be entertained in this regard.

Key Things to Remember Before Applying

  • Ensure you meet the age limit of 21–30 years as on July 6, 2026 - this is the cutoff date, not the notification date
  • Check the essential educational qualification for your chosen post carefully - each post has a different requirement
  • The application email subject line must exactly follow the format: "YP Application – Post Code – Candidate Name" - incorrect subject lines risk non-delivery
  • Only PDF attachments are accepted; total file size must not exceed 5 MB
  • Freshers are eligible - the experience requirements listed are desirable, not mandatory
  • No printouts or hard copies need to be sent by post or courier
  • RBI accepts no responsibility for non-delivery of emails for any technical reason
  • Work experience from the current employer requires a release certificate confirming they can be relieved on short notice if selected

Who Can Apply for RRB Technician 2026?

Eligibility criteria depend on the post and level. Candidates must meet educational, technical, and age requirements as per the Centralised Employment Notification.

  • Technician Grade I Signal: B.Sc. (Physics / Electronics / Computer Science / IT / Instrumentation) or Degree/Diploma in Engineering in relevant discipline from a recognized institution.
  • Technician Grade III: 10th / Matriculation plus ITI from NCVT/SCVT in relevant trade or Act Apprenticeship in the concerned trade.

Salary Details

  • Technician Grade III: Pay Level 2 (7th CPC) – Initial Pay Rs. 19,900/-
  • Additional allowances such as DA, HRA, TA and other benefits will be admissible as per Railway rules for the respective pay levels.

  • Open the link for Centralised Employment Notification CEN 02/2026 – Technician.

  • Register by providing basic details like name, mobile number and email ID.
  • Login using the registration credentials and fill the online application form for the desired post and pay level (only one RRB and one pay level allowed per candidate).
  • Upload required documents, photograph and signature as per specifications. >Pay the prescribed application fee through online mode, if applicable.
  • Submit the application form and take a printout / save PDF for future reference.

Important Points Mentioned in Indicative Notice

  • Separate applications must be submitted for each pay level, if eligible.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

Staff Selection Commission (SSC) has published the Combined Graduate Level Examination Notification 2026 on 21 May 2026. The recruitment drive aims to fill approximately 12,256 Group B and Group C posts across various Ministries and Departments. Candidates within the age range as specified in the official notification and holding a Graduation Degree are eligible to apply online at https://ssc.gov.in. The application process will be active from 21 May 2026 to 22 June 2026, and candidates can easily access the notification PDF and apply link below.

SSC CGL 2026 – Selection Process

Selection is through a two-tier Computer Based Examination (CBE). Marks scored in CBE conducted in multiple shifts will be normalized as per the procedure published by SSC vide Notice dated 02-06-2025. There is no provision for re-evaluation/re-checking of scores at any stage.

Tier-I: Computer Based Examination

Subject No. of Questions Maximum Marks Time
A. General Intelligence & Reasoning 25 50 1 hour (Sectional timer: 15 min per section)
1 hour 20 min for scribe-eligible PwBD candidates
B. General Awareness 25 50
C. Quantitative Aptitude 25 50
D. English Comprehension 25 50
Total 100 200  

Tier-I consists of Objective Type / MCQ questions, set in English and Hindi (except English Comprehension). Negative marking: 0.50 marks per wrong answer.

Tier-II: Computer Based Examination

Tier-II is conducted in Paper-I, Paper-II, and Paper-III in separate shifts/days.

Paper Section / Subject Questions Marks Duration
Paper-I (Compulsory for all posts) Section-I: Mathematical Abilities + Reasoning & General Intelligence 30+30 = 60 180 Session-I: 2 hrs 15 min; Section-I: 1 hr timer
Section-II: English Language & Comprehension + General Awareness 45+25 = 70 210 1 hr timer
Section-III: Computer Knowledge Test (qualifying, mandatory) 20 60 15 min
Section-IV: Data Entry Speed Test (DEST) (qualifying, mandatory) - - Session-II: 15 min
Paper-II (JSO / Statistical Investigator only) Statistics 100 200 2 hours
Paper-III (AAO / AAcO only) General Studies (Finance and Economics) 100 200 2 hours

Negative marking in Tier-II: 1 mark per wrong answer in Section-I, II, III of Paper-I; 0.50 marks in Paper-II and Paper-III. Section-III (CKT) and Section-IV (DEST) are qualifying in nature. Candidates must qualify all sections of Paper-I separately. Higher standards of CKT and DEST are set for specific posts (CSS, MEA, AFHQ, SFIO, CBIC, Postal etc.). Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour is available for PwBD candidates eligible for scribe.

Competition Level Analysis for SSC CGL 2026

The overall competition level for SSC CGL 2026 is expected to remain very high because the examination attracts a massive number of graduate applicants every year across India. Even with around 12,256 vacancies, the effective competition ratio remains extremely tough for high-demand posts.

  1. Applicant volume is huge: SSC CGL is among the most sought-after central government exams, and premium posts receive intense preference from top scorers.
  2. Tier-I acts as the main screening stage: With negative marking and sectional timing, both speed and accuracy matter. Candidates targeting top posts generally need a very strong Tier-I score.
  3. Tier-II gets post-specific: Specialized posts like JSO and AAO attract a smaller but more qualified pool, making domain preparation more important than raw competition numbers.
  4. DEST and CKT can eliminate candidates: Although qualifying in nature, poor performance in these sections can disqualify otherwise strong candidates for certain posts.
  5. Physical standards create an extra filter: Certain Inspector and Sub Inspector posts require physical and medical fitness standards that are checked separately by user departments.

Who Should NOT Apply for SSC CGL 2026?

  1. Candidates who will not possess a Bachelor's Degree by 01-08-2026.
  2. Candidates who fall outside the age limit for all eligible posts even after applicable relaxation.
  3. OBC Creamy Layer candidates intending to claim OBC reservation.
  4. Candidates who cannot meet post-specific physical or medical standards for the posts they plan to prefer.
  5. Non-matriculate Ex-Servicemen or those who have not completed the required length of service.
  6. Candidates applying for JSO without the required Mathematics or Statistics qualification.
  7. Female candidates applying specifically for BRO vacancies, where only male candidates are eligible.
  8. Distance-learning degree holders without valid UGC-DEB approval for the relevant period.

Common Mistakes / What to Check Before Applying SSC CGL 2026

  1. Not generating a fresh OTR on the new SSC website.
  2. Using a pre-existing photograph instead of live photo capture where required.
  3. Uploading blurred or wrongly sized signature files.
  4. Selecting the wrong reservation category without valid supporting certificate.
  5. Ignoring post-specific standards before locking post preferences.
  6. Choosing JSO or AAO related preferences without being ready for Paper-II or Paper-III.
  7. Skipping Aadhaar-based authentication even when eligible.
  8. Waiting until the final date for application submission.
  9. Missing the answer key objection window after examination.
  10. Confusing the correction window fee structure.

How to Apply for SSC CGL 2026

Candidates must apply online only at https://ssc.gov.in or through the mY SSC mobile application (available on Store). No other mode of application is accepted. Candidates who have not generated OTR on the new website must do so first. Once OTR is generated on the new website, it remains valid for all future examinations on that portal.

Candidates are advised to opt for Aadhaar-based authentication during OTR. Aadhaar-authenticated candidates get significant exemptions: their applications are not rejected for photograph/signature standards, and they need not carry photo ID at the examination venue.

Steps to Apply:

  1. Generate One-Time Registration (OTR) at https://ssc.gov.in (mandatory; use Aadhaar-based authentication if possible)
  2. Complete OTR profile and lock it
  3. Fill the Common Application Form (CAF) including live photograph capture via camera
  4. Upload scanned signature (JPEG/JPG, 10–20 KB, 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm)
  5. Fill the Examination Specific Module (post preferences, exam centre choices - 3 centres within same region in order of priority)
  6. Pay application fee of Rs. 100/- online (if applicable) by 23-06-2026
  7. Preview/Print the application to verify all details before final submission
  8. Use the correction window (29-06 to 01-07-2026) if any correction is needed (chargeable)
  9. Keep printout of application and all documents for at least 3 years

Documents to Keep Ready for Document Verification (after final selection):

  • Matriculation/Secondary School Certificate (proof of date of birth)
  • Mark sheets for all years/semesters of Graduation + Provisional/Degree Certificate
  • SC/ST Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure of the notification)
  • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure-X); must be valid as on closing date of application
  • EWS Income & Asset Certificate valid for FY 2026–27 (issued based on income for FY 2025–26) in prescribed format (Annexure-XI)
  • PwBD Disability Certificate from competent authority specifying type of disability (as per Annexure-XII to XIII)
  • Ex-Serviceman discharge certificate and other relevant ESM documents
  • Equivalence certificate (for equivalent qualifications other than standard degrees)
  • DEB/UGC approval letter (for Distance Learning degree holders)
  • Certificate of proficiency in State Regional/official language (for AAO/Assistant Audit Officer State Cadre)

Apply Online at: https://ssc.gov.in | Toll Free Helpline: 1800 309 3063

Important Instructions for SSC CGL 2026 Candidates

  • Final allotment is based on merit-cum-preference, and no alternate post will be offered if a candidate fails post-specific standards after allotment.
  • OBC candidates claiming reservation must not belong to the creamy layer as on the closing date of application.
  • EWS certificate must be valid for FY 2026–27 and should be based on income for FY 2025–26.
  • PwBD candidates must choose the correct sub-category in the application form because no later change is allowed.
  • Scribe rules are strict: the scribe must complete OTR, be Aadhaar-authenticated, and cannot assist more than one candidate.
  • Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour is available to eligible PwBD candidates.
  • Tentative answer keys can be challenged online by paying Rs. 100 per question within the specified period only.
  • No re-evaluation or re-checking of scores is available at any stage.
  • Candidates should preserve the application form and related documents for at least 3 years.
  • Candidature remains provisional until certificates and documents are verified by the Appointing Authority.
  • Fraudulent claims of reservation status may lead to debarment from all SSC examinations.
  • Any update in exam schedule or process will be communicated through the SSC website only.
  • Applications without the required fee, unless exempted, or incomplete applications will be summarily rejected.

How to Apply for Sarkari Job Online 2026

  1. Find the right Sarkari Job: Use the vacancy table or sector links above on OnlyJobs. Filter by your qualification — 10th, 12th, Graduate, or Engineering. Check the last date and eligibility carefully.

  2. Read the official notification: Click on the job listing to open the official notification PDF. Read all eligibility conditions — age limit, educational qualification, experience, category relaxations.

  3. Visit the official recruitment website: Never apply through third-party sites. Use the direct official link provided on OnlyJobs. Look for "Apply Online" or "Register" on the official portal.

  4. Register / Create account: Sign up using your valid email ID and active mobile number. Keep your Aadhaar, bank account details, and email accessible.

  5. Fill the application form: Enter personal details, educational qualifications, category (General/OBC/SC/ST/EWS), address, and other required information accurately.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.
